summary: Garoufalidis, Scholze, Wheeler and Zagier attach to a number field K and R = O_K[1/Δ] (disc(K)·6 | Δ) a Habiro ring H_R of families of power series at the roots of unity that glue p-adically after a Frobenius twist (Definition 1.1), and invertible H_R-modules H_{R,ξ} indexed by ξ ∈ K_3(K), built from the units ε_m(ξ) of Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier and Coleman’s p-adic dilogarithm (Definitions 1.3–1.4). They prove that the local modules are free of rank one (Theorem 1), from the unramified computation D_p : K_3(K_p; Z_p) ≅ p²O_{K_p} for p > 3 (Theorem 9) and explicit Pochhammer sections (Theorem 10), and that H_{R,0} = H_R (Theorem 2). Through the Kontsevich–Soibelman admissibility of the Nahm sums F_A (Theorem 6), its level-m refinement (Theorem 7), the identification with formal Gaussian integration (Theorems 3 and 8) and a Dwork-type Frobenius congruence (Theorem 4), they show that the perturbative series f_{A,z} of a non-degenerate Nahm solution lie in H_{R[δ^{−1/2}],ξ}|_Δ (Theorem 5), with symmetrisations and torsion powers in the Habiro ring (Corollary 1.11, Theorems 11–12). Section 4 works out examples (A = (3), the matrix (8 5; 5 4), 4_1, 5_2 and the (−2,3,7)-pretzel knot, a 5-adic instance of Theorem 9) and Section 5 describes the naive Habiro ring by explicit congruences with index D(N) (Propositions 5.1–5.2) and the number-field ring by Frobenius-twisted congruences (Propositions 5.3–5.4). Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti has Habiro rings, q-Pochhammer symbols, polylogarithms, Bloch groups, higher K-theory or Coleman integration; only tools (Bernoulli polynomials, Picard groups, Teichmüller lifts, completions, CRT, cyclotomic discriminants) are library items. The atlas plans almost everything in HabiroNumberFields HB.1–HB.7, HabiroNahmSeries HB.3–HB.10, HabiroCyclotomicCompletions, HabiroRings and PadicHodgeRegulators D.1–D.4. What is missing (the congruence description of §5, Proposition 5.4, Remarks 3.8 and 5.5, and the Habiro-like series of §5.4) goes as sources to HabiroCyclotomicCompletions, HabiroNumberFields and HabiroNahmSeries, and a fourth source route gives D.3 the corrections to Theorem 9. 83 mistakes are recorded: 49 already in the HabiroNumberFields and HabiroNahmSeries packets, re-checked here, 18 new ones found by the extraction and 16 found by its review, among them the false index in Proposition 5.1 (|det M_N| = D(N − 1)), a gap in the proof of Theorem 9, a failing step in the proof of Dwork’s lemma, the hypothesis δ ∈ R^× missing from Corollary 3.12, and sign or index slips in (109), (166), (253), (254), (273), (285), (287), (323) and (353)–(359). As printed, Definition 1.3 makes Theorem 1 false, and the isomorphism of Theorem 2 is unproved.

items.name: q-Pochhammer symbols
items.statement: (x;q)_n = ∏_{j=0}^{n−1}(1 − q^j x) and (q;q)_n = (1 − q)⋯(1 − q^n); the infinite symbol (x;q)_∞ = ∏_{n≥0}(1 − q^n x) is a formal power series in x over Q(q) with (x;q)_∞^{−1} = Σ_{k≥0} x^k/(q;q)_k.
items.locator: §1.3, p. 4; §1.6, after (28), p. 12; §2.1, first paragraph, p. 18
items.note: HB.8 owns the formal symbol over Q(q); HB.4 the analytic q-Pochhammer products.

items.name: The Habiro ring H
items.statement: H := lim_n Z[q]/(q;q)_n Z[q]. Every element can be written f(q) = Σ_{n≥0} P_{n+1}(q)(q;q)_n with P_n(q) ∈ Z[q], and the expansion becomes unique when deg P_n < n.
items.note: HC.1 plans the cyclotomic completion and the cofinality of the (q;q)_N; HC.2 the normalized factorial expansions.

items.name: The Kontsevich–Zagier series lies in H and its first Taylor coefficients
items.statement: f_{3_1}(q) = Σ_{n≥0}(q;q)_n (the Kashaev invariant of the trefoil) lies in H. With q = ζ_m(1 − u) its expansions begin F_{3_1,1}(u) = 1 + u + 2u² + 5u³ + O(u⁴), F_{3_1,2}(u) = 3 + 11u + O(u²), F_{3_1,3}(u) = 5 − ζ_3 + O(u), F_{3_1,4}(u) = 8 − 3ζ_4 + O(u), and M_5^{−1} applied to their coordinates γ_{m,ℓ,j} gives the integral vector (1 | 1 0 | 1 0 0 | 1 0 0 0); changing γ_{1,1,0} from 1 to 2 destroys integrality.
items.note: HC.6 lists the factorial series Σ P_N as an acceptance example. The expansions and both vectors were rechecked in PARI/GP.

items.name: Compatible system of roots of unity
items.statement: A choice of primitive m-th roots of unity ζ_m, m ≥ 1, with ζ_{mm′} = ζ_m ζ_{m′} for coprime m, m′ and (ζ_{p^r})^p = ζ_{p^{r−1}} for primes p and r ≥ 1, for example ζ_m = exp(2πi Σ_p p^{−v_p(m)}). It satisfies v_p(ζ_{pm} − ζ_m) > 0 for all m and all primes p; the standard choice e^{2πi/m} does not satisfy these relations.

items.name: Galois-invariant functions near roots of unity P_R
items.statement: For a ring R, P_R := (∏_{ζ∈μ_∞} R[ζ][[x]])^{Gal(Q^ab/Q)} ≅ ∏_{m≥1} R[ζ_m][[x]]; an element is a family f(q) = (f_m(x))_m, where q = ζ_m + x, with no convergence assumed. Section 5 uses the local variable u with q = ζ_m(1 − u), x = −ζ_m u.

items.name: Taylor maps ι_m and ι
items.statement: For f ∈ H and q = ζ_m + x one has (q;q)_n ∈ x^{⌊n/m⌋}Z[ζ_m][x], so f(ζ_m + x) ∈ Z[ζ_m][[x]]; this defines ring homomorphisms ι_m : H → Z[ζ_m][[x]] and ι = (ι_m)_m : H → P_Z.

items.name: Injectivity of the Taylor maps and the gluing description of the image
items.statement: ι : H → P_Z and each ι_m are injective (Habiro). The image of ι consists of the families (f_m) satisfying f_m(x + ζ_{pm} − ζ_m) = f_{pm}(x) in Z[ζ_{pm}]^∧_p[[x]] for all m ≥ 1 and all primes p; the re-expansion exists because ζ_{pm} − ζ_m is p-adically small, and each f_m determines the whole family.
items.note: The injectivity is Habiro 2004, Theorems 5.2 and 6.1 (HC.4). The description of the image is not in Habiro 2004 (finding E1).

items.name: The Habiro ring H_R of a number field (Definition 1.1)
items.statement: Let K be a number field, Δ a positive integer divisible by disc(K) (usually also by 6) and R = O_K[1/Δ], so that Z[1/Δ] → R is finite étale. H_R is the set of f = (f_m(x))_{m≥1} ∈ P_R with f_m(x + ζ_{pm} − ζ_m) = (φ_p f_{pm})(x) in R^∧_p[ζ_{pm}][[x]] for all primes p and all m ≥ 1, where φ_p is the Frobenius endomorphism of R^∧_p extended to fix ζ_{pm} and x; the condition is empty for p | Δ because R^∧_p = 0. H_R|_γ is the analogous ring of families on the orders prime to γ, and H_R|_Δ the case γ = Δ.
items.note: Review: Remark 1.8 (p. 13) assumes throughout that only primes p > 3 are considered and that 2 and 3 divide Δ; the items on the modules and on Theorem 5 use this silently.

items.name: H_R is finite étale of rank [K:Q] over H_{Z[1/Δ]}
items.statement: H_R can equivalently be defined as a finite étale H_{Z[1/Δ]}-algebra, obtained by gluing the base changes R[ζ_m][[q − ζ_m]] of Z[ζ_m][[q − ζ_m]] along Frobenius twists after p-adic completion. In particular H_R is a finitely generated projective H_{Z[1/Δ]}-module of rank [K:Q].
items.note: Asserted with a one-line sketch (finding E3). HabiroRings HR.4–HR.5 construct the relative étale Habiro ring and compare it with the explicit ring.

items.name: The p-completed Habiro ring
items.statement: For a prime p, (H_R)^∧_p ≅ {families of R^∧_p[ζ_m][[x]]-series, m ≥ 1, glued by the untwisted re-expansion x ↦ x + ζ_{mp} − ζ_m} ≅ ∏_{m≥1,(m,p)=1} R^∧_p[ζ_m][[x]] ≅ H_{R_p}, the last ring being the naive Habiro ring of R_p.
items.note: Only the middle isomorphism is argued in the paper (finding E6).

items.name: Adelic description of H_R
items.statement: For each prime p there is a commutative square H_R → H_{R^∧_p} over P_R → P_{R^∧_p}, the bottom map being the inclusion followed by φ_p^{v_p(m)} on R^∧_p[ζ_m][[x]]. With R̂ = lim_M R/MR ≅ ∏_p R^∧_p one has H_{R̂} ≅ ∏_p H_{R^∧_p} ≅ H_{Z[1/Δ]} ⊗_Z R̂, and H_R = {f ∈ P_R : φ(f) ∈ H_{R̂}}, i.e. the intersection of φ(P_R) and H_{R̂} inside P_{R̂}, where (φf)_m = φ_m(f_m) with φ_m = ∏_p φ_p^{v_p(m)}.

items.name: Decomposition of H_R over classes of root orders (Remark 1.2)
items.statement: H_R is not a domain when Δ ≠ 1. It is the product, over the classes of Z_{>0} for the equivalence relation generated by m ∼ pm (p ∤ Δ), of the rings of families supported on one class; the factor H_R|_Δ of the class of the orders prime to Δ is an integral domain, but other factors can have non-trivial idempotents when K meets Q(ζ_d).
items.note: Corrected statement; the printed remark calls every factor a domain (findings E4 and E5).

items.name: Abelian fields: R-structure and base change
items.statement: If K is abelian over Q, the lifts φ_p ∈ Gal(K/Q) of the local Frobenius automorphisms (p ∤ Δ) give an embedding R → H_R, a ↦ (φ_m^{−1}a)_m with φ_m = ∏_{p∤Δ} φ_p^{v_p(m)}, and a canonical isomorphism H_R ≅ H_{Z[1/Δ]} ⊗_Z R.
items.note: Corrected exponent −1 (finding E2).

items.name: Odd K-groups of S-integers
items.statement: For r > 1 the localisation map K_{2r−1}(O_K[1/Δ]) → K_{2r−1}(K) is an isomorphism; in particular K_3(R) ≅ K_3(O_K) ≅ K_3(K), which is why the modules are indexed by K_3(K).
items.note: N.2 constructs the localisation sequence and names the odd-degree isomorphism for n ≥ 3 as a separate theorem.

items.name: The Bloch group and its comparison with K_3
items.statement: B(K) is generated by formal combinations Σ_i [x_i], x_i ∈ K^× ∖ {1}, with Σ_i x_i ∧ (1 − x_i) = 0 in ∧²K^×, modulo the five-term relations; K_3(K) ⊗ Q ≅ B(K) ⊗ Q, and Suslin's map K_3(K) → B(K) is surjective.
items.locator: §1.5, pp. 8–9; §3.1, p. 37; proof of Corollary 1.11, p. 44

items.name: The units ε_m(ξ) (mod-m Chern class)
items.statement: For m ≥ 1, ε_m = c²_{ζ_m} : K_3(K) → K(ζ_m)^×/(K(ζ_m)^×)^m (Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier, Theorem 1.5), and (σ_γ ε_m(ξ))^γ/ε_m(ξ) is canonically an m-th power for γ prime to m, σ_γ(ζ_m) = ζ_m^γ (χ^{−1}-equivariance). Equivalently ξ gives a χ^{−1}-equivariant μ_m-torsor over K(ζ_m), from the mod-m étale Chern class K_3(K) ≅ K_3(O_K) → H¹(O_K[1/m], Z/m(2)) → H¹(O_K[1/m, ζ_m], μ_m)^{χ^{−1}}; the torsor is unramified away from m, and the units ε_m(ξ) can be chosen integral at any given finite set of places prime to m.
items.note: Corrected statement (findings E7 and E8).

items.name: Coleman's p-adic dilogarithm D_p
items.statement: After choosing a branch of the logarithm on C_p^× (for example the Iwasawa logarithm, log p = 0), Coleman's analytic continuation along Frobenius gives Li_2 : C_p ∖ {1} → C_p, and D_p(z) = Li_2(z) + ½ log(z) log(1 − z) on C_p ∖ {0,1} satisfies the five-term relation.
items.locator: §1.5, (19), p. 9; §3.1, (172)–(174) and the following paragraph, pp. 37–38
items.note: Review: the combined map D_p : B(K) → K_p is item 91; this item is the function on C_p ∖ {0,1}.

items.name: The p-adic dilogarithm is the p-adic regulator (Besser–de Jeu)
items.statement: Coleman's D_p on K_3 of a number field coincides with the p-adic (syntomic) regulator (Besser–de Jeu, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 36 (2003), Theorem 1.6(2)).

items.name: Invertible L_p(ξ)-sections and the local modules H_{R^∧_p,ξ} (Definition 1.3)
items.statement: Fix ξ ∈ K_3(K) and a prime p ∤ Δ. An invertible L_p(ξ)-section is a family f = (f_m(x))_{m≥1,(m,p)=1} with f_m ∈ ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}(R^∧_p[ζ_m]^× + xR^∧_p[ζ_m] + x²K_p[ζ_m][[x]]) such that log(φ_p f̂(q^p)/f̂(q)^p) ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} (p/x)R^∧_p[ζ_m][[x]], where the formal completion is given by log f̂_m(x) = D_p(ξ)/(m² log q) + log f_m(x) ∈ x^{−1}K_p[ζ_m][[x]]. H_{R^∧_p,ξ} is the H_{R^∧_p}-span of the invertible L_p(ξ)-sections.
items.note: Corrected shape of (20) (finding E9); as printed, Theorem 1 fails.

items.name: Theorem 1: the local modules are free of rank one
items.statement: Let K be a number field and Δ divisible by disc(K) and by 6. For ξ ∈ K_3(K) and a prime p with (p, Δ) = 1, invertible L_p(ξ)-sections exist, and H_{R^∧_p,ξ} is a free H_{R^∧_p}-module of rank 1.
items.note: Holds with the corrected Definition 1.3.

items.name: The global modules H_{R,ξ} (Definition 1.4)
items.statement: For ξ ∈ K_3(K), H_{R,ξ} consists of the families f = (f_m(x))_{m≥1}, f_m ∈ ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}K[ζ_m][[x]], such that for every prime p ∤ Δ the family (f_m)_{(m,p)=1} lies in H_{R^∧_p,ξ} under K → K_p, and f(q^γ)^γ f(q^{−1}) ∈ H_{R[1/γ]}|_γ for every γ ∈ Z_{>0}; here (γ*f)(q) = f(q^γ). The χ^{−1}-equivariance of ε_m removes the ambiguity of the m-th roots in this gluing condition, and the primes p are taken prime to 6.
items.locator: §1.5, Definition 1.4, (23)–(24) and the following paragraph, p. 10
items.note: The quantifier over p is added (finding E10).

items.name: Invertible modules and the Picard group
items.statement: Pic(H_R) is the group, under tensor product, of isomorphism classes of invertible H_R-modules (line bundles on Spec H_R).
items.note: The groupoid-level refinement used in the paper (a module for each ξ, not a class) is not in the libraries.

items.name: Theorem 2(i): H_{R,0} = H_R
items.note: Proved in §3.3. Part (ii), the multiplicative structure, is item 152 (finding E41).

items.name: Abelian fields: a Pochhammer generator of H_{R,ξ}
items.statement: If K ⊂ Q(ζ) and ξ ∈ B(K) is represented by a Gal(Q(ζ)/K)-invariant combination Σ_j n_j[ζ^j] (for example ξ = 2[ζ_6] for the figure-eight knot), then ∏_j (q^{1/2}ζ^j; q)_∞^{n_j} lies in H_{R,ξ} and generates it freely as an H_R-module.
items.note: Stated without proof (finding E11); the local form is Theorem 10.

items.name: Proposition 1.5(a): the involution τ
items.statement: If f ∈ H_{R,ξ} then τf := (−1)*f, τf(q) = f(q^{−1}), lies in H_{R,−ξ}.

items.name: Proposition 1.5(b): pairing and proportionality
items.statement: If f, g ∈ H_{R,ξ} then f·τg ∈ H_R, and there are a, b ∈ H_R with af = bg.
items.note: The proof cites Theorem 2, whose isomorphism statement is not proved (finding E41).

items.name: Proposition 1.5(c): composition of the operations γ*
items.statement: For f ∈ P_R and non-zero integers γ, γ′: (γγ′)*f = γ*(γ′*f).

items.name: Proposition 1.5(d): γ-th powers of γ*f
items.statement: If f ∈ H_{R,ξ} and γ > 0 then (γ*f)^γ ∈ H_{R[1/γ],ξ}|_γ.

items.name: Proposition 1.5(e): vanishing propagates
items.statement: If f ∈ H_{R,ξ} and f_m = 0 for some m, then f_{pm} = 0 for every prime p not dividing Δ.
items.note: A spelling slip in the statement (finding E12).

items.name: Proposition 1.5(f): constant terms
items.statement: If f ∈ H_{R,ξ} and (m, Δ) = 1 then f_m(0) ∈ R[ζ_m, ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}].

items.name: Admissible series (Kontsevich–Soibelman)
items.statement: For t = (t_1, …, t_N), a series F(t,q) ∈ Q(q)[[t]] with F = 1 + O(t) is admissible if log F(t,q) = −Σ_{0≠n∈Z_{≥0}^N} Σ_{ℓ≥1} L_n(q^ℓ)/(ℓ(1 − q^ℓ)) t^{ℓn} with every L_n(q) ∈ Z[q^{±1}].

items.name: Admissibility and Donaldson–Thomas exponents
items.statement: Every F ∈ Z((q))[[t]] with F(0,q) = 1 has a unique expansion F = ∏_{0≠n} ∏_{i∈Z} (q^i t^n; q)_∞^{c_{n,i}}, c_{n,i} ∈ Z, with c_{n,i} = 0 for i ≪ 0; F is admissible if and only if for each n only finitely many c_{n,i} are non-zero, and then L_n(q) = Σ_i c_{n,i} q^i.
items.locator: §1.6, (28)–(29), p. 12; proof of Theorem 6, first paragraph, p. 24
items.note: The existence of the expansion is argued by induction on the t-degree (finding E25).

items.name: Expansions of an admissible series at roots of unity
items.statement: To an admissible F attach the family f(t,q) = (f_m(t,x))_{m≥1}, f_m(t,x) = F(t^{1/m}, ζ_m + x).

items.name: The Nahm sums F_A and their congruence sums F_{A,m,k}
items.statement: For a symmetric integral N×N matrix A, F_A(t,q) = Σ_{n∈Z_{≥0}^N} (−1)^{diag(A)·n} q^{½(nᵀAn + diag(A)·n)} t^n/((q;q)_{n_1}⋯(q;q)_{n_N}); for m ≥ 1 and k ∈ {0,…,m−1}^N, F_{A,m,k}(t,q) = Σ_{n∈k+mZ_{≥0}^N} (−1)^{diag(A)·(n−k)} q^{½(nᵀAn − kᵀAk) + ½diag(A)·(n−k)} t^{n−k}/∏_j (q^{k_j+1};q)_{n_j−k_j}. The original Nahm sums are the specialisations t = (−1)^{diag(A)}q^b of positive-definite A.

items.name: The q-difference system of F_A
items.statement: F_A(t,q) − F_A(σ_j t, q) = (−1)^{A_{jj}} t_j q^{A_{jj}} F_A(∏_i σ_i^{A_{ij}} t, q), j = 1, …, N, where σ_j multiplies t_j by q; together with F_A(0,q) = 1 this system determines F_A.

items.name: The t-deformed Nahm equations and the rings S, S^{(m)}
items.statement: 1 − z_j(t) = (−1)^{A_{jj}} t_j ∏_i z_i(t)^{A_{ij}}, z_j(0) = 1, j = 1, …, N, has a unique solution z(t) ∈ Z[[t]]^N; δ(t) := ∏_j z_j(t)^{−A_{jj}} det(diag(1 − z(t))A + diag(z(t))) is its discriminant; S = Z[t^{±1}, z^{±1}, δ^{−1/2}]/(1 − z − (−1)^A t z^A), étale over Z[t] after inverting 2, and S^{(m)} = Z[ζ_m, t^{±1/m}, z^{±1}, δ^{−1/2}]/(the same relations), S^{(1)} = S.
items.note: Corrected index z_i in (34) (finding E13).

items.name: Theorem 3: admissible and formal-Gaussian series coincide
items.statement: For every symmetric integral matrix A, f_A(t,q) = f_A^{FGI}(t,q) as families of series at all roots of unity.
items.locator: §1.7, Theorem 3, (38), p. 14; refined as Theorem 8, p. 35

items.name: Theorem 4: Frobenius congruence for the congruence sums
items.statement: For a symmetric integral A, m ≥ 1, k ∈ {0,…,m−1}^N and every prime p with (m, p) = 1: log F_{A,m,k}(t^{p/m}, q^p) − p log F_{A,m,k}(t^{1/m}, q) ∈ (p/x) S^{(m)}[z(t)^{1/m}]^∧_p[[x]], q = ζ_m + x.
items.note: The last step of the proof needs an argument (finding E37).

items.name: Nahm equations, non-degenerate solutions and their Bloch elements
items.statement: At t = 1: 1 − z_j = (−1)^{A_{jj}} ∏_i z_i^{A_{ij}}, with R[δ^{−1/2}] = Z[z^{±1}, δ^{−1/2}]/(Nahm equations) and the specialisation S → R[δ^{−1/2}], t ↦ 1, compatible with the Frobenius t ↦ t^p. A non-degenerate solution is an isolated solution with δ ≠ 0; it generates a number field K and defines ξ = Σ_j [z_j] ∈ B(K).
items.note: Corrected index in (41) (finding E13).

items.name: The family f_{A,z}(q) of a non-degenerate Nahm solution
items.statement: f_{A,z}(q) = (f_{A,z,m}(x))_m is the specialisation of f_A(t,q) at t = 1 along the solution z, after removing the principal part of the logarithm.

items.name: The potential specialises to the p-adic dilogarithm
items.statement: For p ∤ Δ, V(t) specialises under t = 1 to D_p(ξ), and V(t^p) = φ_p V(t) specialises to D_p(φ_p ξ) = φ_p D_p(ξ).
items.note: Asserted without proof (finding E14).

items.name: The restricted modules H_{R,ξ}|_Δ
items.statement: H_{R,ξ}|_Δ is the set of families indexed by the roots of unity of order prime to Δ that satisfy the conditions of Definition 1.4 (the local conditions at every p ∤ Δ and the gluing (24)) on those orders; H_{R,0}|_Δ = H_R|_Δ.
items.note: Corrected: the printed definition refers to the ring gluing (13) (finding E15).

items.name: Theorem 5: perturbative series lie in the Habiro modules
items.statement: Let A be a symmetric integral N×N matrix and z a non-degenerate solution of the Nahm equations (41) (isolated, δ ≠ 0); let K = Q(z), ξ = Σ_j [z_j] ∈ B(K), and R = O_K[1/Δ] with Δ divisible by disc(K), by 6, by the finitely many exceptional primes of Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier Theorem 1.6 for K, and such that every z_j ∈ R^×. Then f_{A,z}(q) ∈ H_{R[δ^{−1/2}],ξ}|_Δ.
items.note: Findings E14, E42, E43, E44 and E45 concern the proof.

items.name: Remark 1.9: expected strengthenings
items.statement: Theorem 5 is expected without the restriction to orders prime to Δ, and follows if Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier Theorem 1.6 holds for all m; under √δ ↦ −√δ the element f_{A,z} lies in the −1-eigenspace; the results extend to rational A through m-admissible series, with more primes in Δ.
items.note: Conditional or expected statements.

items.name: Corollary 1.10: constant terms of f_{A,z}
items.statement: For m prime to Δ the constant term of f_{A,z} at ζ_m lies in R[δ^{−1/2}][ζ_m, ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}]. For the figure-eight knot, (1/√(m*)) Σ_{k∈Z/mZ} (ζ_mθ; ζ_m)_k (ζ_m^{−1}θ^{−1}; ζ_m^{−1})_k ∈ Z[ζ_{6m}] for θ^m = ζ_6, (m, 6) = 1, m* = (−1)^{(m−1)/2}m.
items.note: Corrected statement (findings E16 and E17).

items.name: Corollary 1.11(a): the symmetrisation lies in a Habiro ring
items.statement: For A, z as in Theorem 5, f_{A,z}(q) f_{A,z}(q^{−1}) ∈ H_{R[δ^{−1}]}, which is H_R when δ ∈ R^×.
items.note: Corrected statement (finding E18).

items.name: Corollary 1.11(b): torsion powers lie in the Habiro ring
items.statement: If rξ = 0 in K_3(K) for some r > 0, then f_{A,z}(q)^r ∈ H_{R[δ^{−1/2}]}.

items.name: Bloch-torsion criterion
items.statement: If ξ is torsion of order r, then f_{A,z}(q)^r ∈ H_{R[δ^{−1/2}]} (Corollary 1.11(b)), so f_{A,z}(q)^{2r} ∈ H_{R[δ^{−1/2}]} (the paper writes H_R, which needs δ ∈ R^×; finding E18). Conversely, if some power f_{A,z}^n lies in H_{R[δ^{−1}]} and f_{A,z,ℓ}(0) ≠ 0 for infinitely many primes ℓ ∤ Δ, then ξ is torsion.
items.note: Corrected converse (finding E19).

items.name: Neumann–Zagier data and their Nahm matrices
items.statement: A Neumann–Zagier datum of an ideal triangulation consists of the upper half (A|B) (A, B ∈ M_N(Z)) of a symplectic integral 2N×2N matrix, a vector ν ∈ Z^N and a solution z of ∏_j z_j^{A_{ij}}(1 − 1/z_j)^{B_{ij}} = (−1)^{ν_i}. When B is invertible over Z, I − B^{−1}A is a symmetric integral matrix, the Neumann–Zagier equations are equivalent to the Nahm equations, and the perturbative series of complex Chern–Simons theory defined by formal Gaussian integration match those of Theorem 5; such a choice of quads exists for all knots with at most 14 crossings (SnapPy triangulations).
items.locator: §1.8, (45) and the following paragraphs, pp. 15–17; Remark 4.2, p. 48
items.note: See finding E75.

items.name: Two expansions of log(t;q)_∞ and the Dwork-type differences
items.statement: log(t;q)_∞ = −Σ_{ℓ≥1} t^ℓ/(ℓ(1 − q^ℓ)) = Σ_{k≥0} (B_k/k!) Li_{2−k}(t) log(1+x)^{k−1} (q = 1 + x), and for every prime p: log(t^p; q^p)_∞ − p log(t;q)_∞ = p Σ_{ℓ≥1, p∤ℓ} t^ℓ/(ℓ(1 − q^ℓ)) = −p Σ_{k≥0} (B_k/k!) Li^{(p)}_{2−k}(t) log(1+x)^{k−1}.

items.name: The p-part of the polylogarithm
items.statement: Li^{(p)}_n(t) = Li_n(t) − p^{−n}Li_n(t^p) = Σ_{k≥1, p∤k} t^k/k^n.

items.name: Coleman's integrality of Li^{(p)}_n
items.statement: Li^{(p)}_n(t) ∈ Z_(p)[[t]] converges for |t/(1 − t)| < p^{(p−1)^{−1}} and lies in the ring Z[t/(1 − t)]^∧_p of series in Z_p[[t]] convergent for |t/(1 − t)| ≤ 1 (Coleman 1982, Proposition 6.2).
items.note: Cited; the paper uses only Lemma 2.1.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: Li^{(p)}_n ∈ Z[t, 1/(1 − t)]^∧_p
items.statement: For every integer n and prime p, Li^{(p)}_n(t) ∈ Z[t, 1/(1 − t)]^∧_p.
items.note: The period in (54) is p^{N+1} (finding E20).

items.name: Proposition 2.2(a): the Dwork difference of the Pochhammer symbol
items.statement: For every prime p, log(t^p; q^p)_∞ − p log(t;q)_∞ ∈ (p/x) Z[t, 1/(1 − t)]^∧_p[[x]], q = 1 + x.

items.name: Proposition 2.2(b): its value at roots of unity
items.statement: For a root of unity ζ ∈ C_p ∖ {1} of order not a power of p, log(ζ^p; q^p)_∞ − p log(ζ; q)_∞ ∈ −p Li^{(p)}_2(ζ)/x + pZ_p[ζ][[x]], q = 1 + x; the function is meromorphic on |x| < 1 with a simple pole at x = 0 of the stated residue.
items.note: Corrected sign and ring (finding E21).

items.name: Expansion of the Pochhammer symbol at all roots of unity
Bernoulli numbers and polynomials
items.statement: The Bernoulli polynomials are given by x e^{xy}/(e^x − 1) = Σ_k B_k(y)x^k/k!, with B_0(y) = 1, B_1(y) = y − ½ and B_k = B_k(0), so B_1 = −½.
items.note: Mathlib's bernoulli has B_1 = −½, matching the paper.

items.name: Closure properties of admissible series
items.statement: Products of admissible series are admissible, and F(t,q) is admissible if and only if F(t,q^{−1}) is admissible.

items.name: Integrality of the ratio and the symmetrisation
items.statement: For admissible F, G(t,q) = F(qt,q)/F(t,q) and F^{sym}(t,q) = F(t,q)F(t,q^{−1}) lie in Z[q^{±1}][[t]]; explicitly G = ∏_{n}∏_i (q^i t^n; q)_{n_1+⋯+n_N}^{−c_{n,i}} and F^{sym} = ∏_n∏_i (q^{1−i}t^n; q)_{2i−1}^{−c_{n,i}}, using (1 − t)(qt;q)_∞ = (t;q)_∞ and (t;q^{−1})_∞ = 1/(qt;q)_∞.

items.name: The potential V, the discriminant δ and the constants U_m of an admissible series
items.note: Corrected sign and ring in (67) (finding E22).

items.name: Lemma 2.3: the shape of the expansions of an admissible series
items.statement: For every m, f_m(t,x) ∈ e^{V(t)/(m² log(1+x/ζ_m))} δ(t)^{−1/2} U_m(t)(1 + x t^{1/m}Q[ζ_m][[t^{1/m}]][[x]]), and f_m(0,x) = 1.
items.note: The residue in (70) carries the factor ζ_m (finding E23).

items.name: Corollary 2.4(a): V is determined by the values L_n(1)
items.statement: For admissible F^{(1)}, F^{(2)} in the same variables t: V^{(1)} = V^{(2)} if and only if L^{(1)}_n(1) = L^{(2)}_n(1) for all n.

items.name: Lemma 2.5: the Dwork quotient of an admissible series
items.statement: If F is admissible, then log(F(t^p,q^p)/F(t,q)^p) = pΣ_n Σ_{(p,ℓ)=1} L_n(q^ℓ)t^{ℓn}/(ℓ(1 − q^ℓ)), and for all primes p and m prime to p, log F(t^{p/m}, q^p) − p log F(t^{1/m}, q) ∈ (p/x) Z_(p)[t^{1/m}, ζ_m][[t, x]], q = ζ_m + x.

items.name: The solution of the t-deformed Nahm equations is hypergeometric
items.statement: The system (34) has a unique solution z(t) ∈ Z[[t]]^N with z(0) = 1 (Rodriguez Villegas). For N = 1 it is z(t) = Σ_{k≥0} (−1)^{(A+1)k} binom(Ak,k)/((A−1)k + 1) t^k, with z(t)^s = sΣ_k (−1)^{(A+1)k} binom(Ak+s−1,k)/((A−1)k + s) t^k and log z(t) = Σ_{k≥1} (−1)^{(A+1)k} binom(Ak,k)/(Ak) t^k; z is algebraic with singularities at t = 0, ∞ and, for A ≥ 2, t = (−1)^{A+1}(A−1)^{A−1}/A^A.
items.note: Corrected singular point (finding E24).

items.name: The involution identity F_A(t,q) = F_{I−A}(t,q^{−1})
Lemma 2.6: the polar part of log F_A
items.statement: For every symmetric integral N×N matrix A there is V_A(t) ∈ Q[[t]] with log F_A(t, ζ_m + x) = ζ_m V_A(t^m)/(m²x) + O(x⁰) for all m ≥ 1; for N = 1 and A a positive integer, V_A(t) = −Li_2(1 − z(t)) − (A/2)log(z(t))² = Σ_{k≥1} (−1)^{(A+1)k} binom(Ak,k) t^k/(Ak²).

items.name: Theorem 6: the Nahm sums F_A are admissible (Kontsevich–Soibelman, Efimov)
items.statement: For an integral symmetric N×N matrix A, the unique c_{n,i} ∈ Z with F_A(t,q) = ∏_{0≠n}∏_{i∈Z}(q^i t^n; q)_∞^{c_{n,i}} have finite support: for each n, c_{n,i} = 0 for all but finitely many i.
items.note: Findings E25, E26 and E27 concern the proof.

items.name: Lemma 2.7: the level-m plethystic logarithm
items.statement: Every F(t,q) ∈ 1 + tZ[1/m]((q))[[t]] can be written uniquely as exp(−Σ_{n≥1}Σ_{ℓ≥1,(ℓ,m)=1} L_n(q^ℓ)t^{nℓ}/(ℓ(1 − q^{mℓ}))) with L_n(q) ∈ Z[1/m]((q)), and conversely; the proof uses exp(−Σ_{(ℓ,m)=1} q^{kℓ}t^{nℓ}/(ℓ(1 − q^{mℓ}))) = ∏_{d|m}(q^{dk}t^{dn}; q^{dm})_∞^{μ(d)/d}.

items.name: Level-m admissible series (Definition 2.8)
items.statement: A series F(t,q) ∈ 1 + tZ[1/m]((q))[[t]] is m-admissible if the L_n(q) of Lemma 2.7 satisfy L_n(q) ∈ Z[1/m, q^{±1}, Φ_d(q)^{−1} | d ≢ 0 (mod m)] and L_n(ζ_m) ∈ Z[1/m]; level 1 is Kontsevich–Soibelman admissibility.
items.note: With this ring Theorem 7 fails; see the corrected Theorem 7 and finding E28.

items.name: The polar parts of the logarithm of an m-admissible series
items.statement: At ζ_m the polar part of log F is ζ_m V(t)/(m²x) with V(t)/m² = Σ_nΣ_{(ℓ,m)=1} L_n(ζ_m^ℓ)t^{nℓ}/(mℓ²); at ζ_{am} with gcd(a,m) = 1 it is ζ_{am}V(t^a)/(a²m²x); at ζ_{am} with gcd(a,m) > 1 it comes from poles of the L_n.
items.note: Corrected statement (finding E29).

items.name: Lemma 2.9: the polar part of the congruence sums
items.statement: For A symmetric integral, V = V_A as in Lemma 2.6, m > 0 and k ∈ {0,…,m−1}^N: log F_{A,m,k}(t, ζ_m + x) = ζ_m V(t^m)/(m²x) + O(x⁰).

items.name: Theorem 7: the congruence sums are level-m admissible
items.statement: For A symmetric integral, m ≥ 1 and k ∈ {0,…,m−1}^N, F_{A,m,k}(t^{1/m}, q) ∈ 1 + tZ[1/m]((q))[[t]] has L_n(q) in Z[1/m, q^{±1}, Φ_d^{−1} : m ∤ d, or m | d and gcd(d/m, m) > 1] with L_n(ζ_m) ∈ Z[1/m].
items.note: Corrected ring (finding E28); finding E30 (the sign in (98)) concerns the proof.

items.name: Lemma 2.10: the Dwork quotient of an m-admissible series
items.statement: For an m-admissible F, all primes p and m′ with (mm′, p) = 1: log F(t^{p/m′}, q^p) − p log F(t^{1/m′}, q) ∈ (p/x) Z_(p)[t^{1/mm′}, ζ_{mm′}][[t, x]], q = ζ_{mm′} + x.
items.note: The exponents in (109) are misprinted (finding E31).

items.name: Formal Gaussian integration
items.statement: For a Q-algebra R and a symmetric N×N matrix Λ over R that is invertible over R (the paper says 'with integer entries', but applies the bracket to Λ(t^m) over S^{(m)}_Q), ⟨f(w,h)⟩_Λ := exp((h/2)Σ_{i,j}(Λ^{−1})_{ij}∂_{w_i}∂_{w_j}) f(w,h)|_{w=0} ∈ R[[h]] for f ∈ R[[w, w³h^{−1}, h]]; formally it is the normalised integral ∫e^{−wᵀΛw/(2h)} f dw / ∫e^{−wᵀΛw/(2h)} dw.

items.name: The modified Pochhammer factor ψ_{k,z,ζ_m} and the critical value V^{FGI}
items.statement: With h = log(1 + x/ζ_m): ψ_{k,z,ζ_m}(w,x) = ((ζ_m+x)^{k+1}ze^w; ζ_m+x)_∞ · exp(−Li_2(z^m)/(m²h) − Li_1(z^m)w/(mh) − Li_0(z^m)w²/(2h) − Σ_{ℓ=0}^{m−1}(½ − (k+ℓ+1)/m) log(1 − ζ_m^{k+ℓ+1}z)). This removes from the logarithm the w⁰, w¹, w² parts of the h^{−1} term and the constant h⁰ term, so ψ ∈ Q(z,ζ_m)[[w, w³x^{−1}, x]] with constant term 1. (114) as printed has m² in the w and w² denominators and the opposite sign on the last sum. The phase (115) has critical points w = (1/m)log z(t^m) and critical value V^{FGI}(t^m)/m², where V^{FGI}(t) = −Σ_j Li_2(1 − z_j(t)) − ½Σ_{i,j}A_{ij} log z_i(t) log z_j(t) (116).
items.note: Review: the statement uses the corrected (114); the printed version is finding E76. Checked numerically for m = 1, 2, 3.

items.name: The formal-Gaussian series f^{FGI}_{A,m} (Definition 2.11)
items.statement: f^{FGI}_{A,m}(t,x) = Σ_{k∈(Z/mZ)^N} I_{A,m,k}(t^{1/m}, x), where I_{A,m,k} is the formal Gaussian integral (118) with Λ(t) = −A − diag(z(t)/(1 − z(t))); I_{A,m,k} is m-periodic in k.
items.note: The m-periodicity is asserted with references to Bar-Natan–Garoufalidis–Rozansky–Thurston and Garoufalidis–Storzer–Wheeler.

items.name: δ^{FGI}, U^{FGI}_m and the cyclic dilogarithm D_{ζ_m}
items.note: Corrected phase in (121) (finding E32).

items.name: Lemma 2.12: algebraicity of the formal-Gaussian series
items.statement: For every m, log f^{FGI}_{A,m}(t,x) ∈ V^{FGI}(t)/(m² log(1 + x/ζ_m)) − ½ log δ^{FGI}(t) + log U^{FGI}_m(t) + xS^{(m)}_Q[[x]], with δ^{FGI}(t) ∈ S and m^{Nm}U^{FGI}_m(t)^{2m} ∈ S^{(m)}.

items.name: The cyclic dilogarithm at 1
items.note: The paper refers to the multiplier system of the Dedekind η-function; checked directly for m = 2, 3. Mathlib has η (mathlib:ModularForm.eta) but not its multiplier system.

items.name: The congruence formal-Gaussian sums Ω^{FGI}_{A,m,k}
items.statement: For m′ prime to m and k ∈ (Z/mZ)^N, Ω^{FGI}_{A,m,k}(t,q) is the sum over ℓ ∈ (Z/mm′Z)^N with ℓ ≡ k (mod m) of (q;q)_{k_1}⋯(q;q)_{k_N} I_{A,mm′,ℓ}(t^{1/m},x) divided by (−1)^{diag(A)·k}q^{½(kᵀAk + diag(A)·k)}t^{k/m}, q = ζ_{mm′} + x; Ω^{FGI}_{A,1,0}(t, ζ_{m′} + x) = f^{FGI}_A(t^{m′}, ζ_{m′} + x).

items.name: Lemma 2.13: the Dwork quotient of the formal-Gaussian congruence sums
items.statement: For all primes p and m prime to p, log Ω^{FGI}_{A,m,k}(t^p,q^p) − p log Ω^{FGI}_{A,m,k}(t,q) ∈ x^{−1}S^{(m)}_p[1/p, z^{1/m}][[x]], q = ζ_m + x; the proof shows V(t^p)/p − pV(t) ∈ pS^{(1)}_p and the analogous statement for δ^{−1}U^2_{m,k}.
items.note: Signs in (132)–(135) (finding E33).

items.name: Remark 2.14: the Dwork quotient of f^{FGI}_A when U^{FGI}_m is a unit
items.statement: If U^{FGI}_m(t) is a p-unit then log f^{FGI}_A(t^p,q^p) − p log f^{FGI}_A(t,q) ∈ x^{−1}S^{(m)}_p[1/p][[x]], q = ζ_m + x.

items.name: Lemma 2.15: the q-difference equations of the congruence sums
items.statement: t^k Ω^{FGI}_{A,m,k}(t^m, q) satisfies Σ_{ℓ=0}^m (−1)^ℓ q^{−ℓ(ℓ−1)/2} binom(m,ℓ)_{q^{−1}} σ_j^ℓ(t^kΩ(t^m,q)) = (−1)^{A_{jj}m} q^{A_{jj}m(m+1)/2} t_j^m ∏_i σ_i^{mA_{ij}}(t^kΩ(t^m,q)), j = 1, …, N.
items.note: Corrected sign and index (finding E30).

items.name: Lemma 2.16: the WKB coefficients are algebraic (rank one)
items.statement: For a 1×1 integer matrix A, let F(t;h) ∈ Q((h))[[t]] be the unique solution with F(0;h) = 1 of F(t;h) − F(e^h t;h) = tF(e^{Ah}t;h). Let z ∈ Z[[t]] solve 1 − z = tz^A with z(0) = 1, and set X = (z − 1)/((1 − A)z + A) and ∆ = X(AX + 1)((A − 1)X + 1). Then the coefficients b_k(t) defined by G(t;h) = F(e^h t;h)/F(t;h) = z(t)exp(Σ_{k≥1}b_k(t)h^k) exist, b_1 = (A(A − 1)/2)X², and b_k ∈ X∆Q[X] for k > 1.
items.note: An outline for N = 1 only, an alternative to Lemma 2.12.

items.name: Corollary 2.17: the WKB expansion of F
items.statement: The coefficients c_k(t) of log F(t;h) = Σ_{k≥−1} c_k(t)h^k exist and c_k(t) ∈ XQ[X] for k > 0.

items.name: Theorem 8: congruence sums equal formal-Gaussian sums
items.statement: For every symmetric integral A, m ≥ 1, k ∈ {0,…,m−1}^N and m′ prime to m: F_{A,m,k}(t^{1/m}, q) = Ω^{FGI}_{A,m,k}(t,q) in Q[ζ_{mm′}]((x))[[t]], q = ζ_{mm′} + x.
items.note: Restricted to m′ prime to m (finding E34); findings E30 and E35 concern (165)–(166). The proof is written for N = 1 and says the general case is identical.

items.name: The admissible and formal-Gaussian invariants coincide
items.statement: For every symmetric integral A, the invariants of the admissible series F_A ((65)–(67)) coincide with the formal-Gaussian ones ((116), (120), (121)): δ_A = δ^{FGI}, V_A = V^{FGI} and U_{A,m} = U^{FGI}_m for all m ≥ 1 (with (67) and (121) corrected).
items.note: With (67) and (121) corrected (findings E22 and E32).

items.name: Corollary 2.18: V determines A
items.statement: If V = V_A is the potential of F_A, then t_j∂_{t_j}V(t) = log z_j(t), and (t_i∂_{t_i})(t_j∂_{t_j})V = (Λ(t)^{−1})_{ij} with Λ = −A − diag(z/(1 − z)); hence V determines z, A and F_A.
items.note: Corrected Hessian identity (finding E36).

items.name: The integrality step in the proof of Theorem 4
items.note: The argument covers only uncompleted elements (finding E37).

items.name: The dilogarithm and the Bloch–Wigner function
items.statement: Li_2(x) = Σ_{k≥1}x^k/k² for |x| < 1; the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm is D(z) = Im Li_2(z) + arg(1 − z) log|z|; for an embedding σ : K → C, D_σ : B(K) → R is the linear extension of [z] ↦ D(σ(z)).
items.note: The continuity of D and the five-term relation, which make D_σ well defined on B(K), are item 156.

items.name: The combined p-adic dilogarithm D_p : B(K) → K_p
items.statement: For p unramified in K the maps D_σ, σ : K → C_p, combine into one map D_p : B(K) → K_p whose projections to the field factors of K_p are the D_σ; R = O_K[1/Δ] and R^∧_p is its p-adic completion.
items.note: Review: distinct from item 17, which is the function D_p on C_p ∖ {0,1}; defined only for p unramified in K (p ∤ Δ).

items.name: Lemma 3.1: p²-integrality of the p-adic dilogarithm
items.statement: Let p > 3 with p ∤ Δ (so p is unramified in K). If z ∈ R^∧_p with |z|_p = 1 and |z − 1|_p ≥ 1 in every factor of R^∧_p, then D_p(z) ∈ p²R^∧_p.
items.note: The hypotheses p > 3 unramified are used in the proof; the Taylor expansion step was rechecked. The proof rests on the cited (175), item 157; the extraction had stated (175) as an 'in particular' consequence, which reverses the logic.

items.name: Kontsevich's finite polylogarithm
items.statement: li_{n,p}(z) = Σ_{k=1}^{p−1} z^k/k^n; Q_{p^s} is the unramified extension of Q_p of degree s and Z_{p^s} its ring of integers.

items.name: Proposition 3.2: reduction of the p-adic dilogarithm (Besser)
items.statement: For a prime p and ζ ∈ μ(Q_{p^s}) of order prime to p with ζ ≠ 1: p^{−2}D_p(ζ^p) ≡ li_{2,p}(ζ)/(ζ − 1)^p (mod p) (Besser, Compositio Math. 130 (2002), Cor. 2.2).
items.note: Review: The printed statement allows p = 2, ζ = −1, where D_p(ζ^p) = D_p(1) is undefined; for odd p every element of μ(Q_{p^s}) has order prime to p. Only p > 3 is used (Proposition 3.3). See finding E80.

items.name: Proposition 3.3: dilogarithms of roots of unity span Z_{p^s}
items.statement: For p > 3 and every s ≥ 1, Span_{Z_p}{p^{−2}D_p(ζ) | ζ ∈ μ(Q_{p^s}), ζ ≠ 1} = Z_{p^s}.
items.note: ζ = 1 excluded (finding E38). The printed statement has no condition on p; p > 3 is needed in the proof (li_{2,p}(1) ≡ 0 (mod p) fails for p = 3, where li_{2,3}(1) ≡ 2) and is the only case used (Theorem 9).

items.name: Roots of unity of an unramified extension (Teichmüller)
items.statement: For p odd, reduction modulo p gives an isomorphism μ(Q_{p^s}) ≅ F_{p^s}^×, μ(Q_{p^s}) = μ_{p^s−1}: every non-zero element of F_{p^s} has a unique lift to Z_{p^s} that is a (p^s − 1)-th root of unity (its Teichmüller lift). (For p = 2, μ(Q_{2^s}) = {±1} × μ_{2^s−1}.)
items.note: Review: the Tau Ceti declarations give μ_{q−1}(O_K) ≅ k^× for a nonarchimedean local field; that an unramified extension of Q_p, p odd, has no further roots of unity (Q_{p^s}(ζ_p)/Q_{p^s} is ramified) is a one-line addition.

items.name: Local K-theory of an unramified product
items.statement: If p is unramified in K, p = ∏_i p_i with N(p_i) = p^{s_i}, then K_p ≅ ∏_i Q_{p^{s_i}} and K_n(K_p) ≅ ∏_i K_n(Q_{p^{s_i}}) for every n.
items.note: The cited computation of K_3(K_p; Z_p) is item 158.

items.name: Theorem 9(a): the local K_3 calculation
items.statement: Assume p > 3 and p unramified in K. Then D_p : K_3(K_p; Z_p) → p²O_{K_p} is a Z_p-linear isomorphism.
items.note: The printed theorem says only 'Assume p > 3'; p unramified is implicit, since D_p : B(K) → K_p is defined only for unramified p (p. 38). Part (b), generation by roots of unity, is item 155. Finding E39 concerns the proof of this part.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: Dwork's lemma
items.statement: Let p be a prime, m prime to p, S a p-complete torsion-free ring with a Frobenius lift φ_p (φ_p(ζ_m) = ζ_m^p, φ_p(x) = x), and f(x) ∈ 1 + xS[1/p, ζ_m][[x]]. Then f ∈ 1 + xS[ζ_m][[x]] if and only if φ_p(f)((ζ_m + x)^p − ζ_m^p)/f(x)^p ∈ 1 + pxS[ζ_m][[x]] and f ∈ 1 + xS[ζ_m] + O(x²).
items.note: The coefficient in (188) and the telescoping (190) need correcting (finding E40).

items.name: Corollary 3.5: exponentials of Dwork-integral logarithms
items.statement: Fix an odd prime p and a p-complete torsion-free ring S with a Frobenius lift φ_p (φ_p(ζ_m) = ζ_m^p). Let g = (g_m)_{(m,p)=1}, g_m ∈ S[1/p, ζ_m][[x]], with φ_p g(q^p) − p g(q) ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} pS[ζ_m][[q − ζ_m]]. Then f = exp(g) is defined, and if f(ζ_m + x) ∈ (1 + pS[ζ_m]) + xS[ζ_m] + O(x²) then f ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} S[ζ_m][[q − ζ_m]].
items.note: Review: Printed for every prime p; for p = 2 exp(g) need not converge (S = Z_2, m = 1, g = 2), so p odd is required (only p > 3 is used). The proof's step 'g_m(0) ∈ pS[ζ_m]' uses that φ_p(a) ∈ pS forces a ∈ pS, true for S = R^∧_p with p unramified (the case used). See finding E79.

items.name: Lemma 3.6: normalising the extension to all roots of unity
items.statement: Let p > 3 be a prime with p ∤ Δ, ξ ∈ K_3(K), and f = (f_m)_{m≥1} with f_m ∈ ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}(R^∧_p[ζ_m]^× + xR^∧_p[ζ_m] + x²K_p[ζ_m][[x]]) such that φ_p f̂(q^p)/f̂(q)^p ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} exp((p/x)R^∧_p[ζ_m][[x]]), with f̂ as in (22). Then for each m prime to p there is a unique β_m ∈ Z_p such that f̃_{mp^d}(x) = ζ_{p^d}^{β_m}f_{mp^d}(x) satisfies f̃(q^σ)/f̃(q)^{σ^{−1}} ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} R^∧_p[ζ_m][[x]] for all σ ∈ Z_p^×.
items.note: Review: The printed lemma says 'Fix a prime p'; the proof needs p ≠ 2, 3 (ω − ω^{−1} ∈ Z_p^× for a generator ω of μ_{p−1}). In the proof, β_m = −α_ω/(ω − ω^{−1}), where α_σ is the exponent in (199).

items.name: Corollary 3.7: unique extension of a local section to all roots of unity
items.statement: Let p > 3 with p ∤ Δ. An invertible L_p(ξ)-section f (Definition 1.3) has a unique lift to a family f = (f_m(x))_{m≥1} with f_m(x) ∈ R^∧_p[ζ_m]^{×/m} + xK_p[ζ_m][[x]] (203) satisfying φ_p f̂(q^p)/f̂(q)^p ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} exp((p/x)R^∧_p[ζ_m][[x]]) and f(q^σ)/f(q)^{σ^{−1}} ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1} R^∧_p[ζ_m][[x]] for all σ ∈ Z_p^×, with f̂ as in (22).
items.note: Review: No proof is printed; it follows from Corollary 3.5 and Lemma 3.6 and so inherits p > 3. The notation R^∧_p[ζ_m]^{×/m} is the paper's (presumably ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}R^∧_p[ζ_m]^× as in (195)).

items.name: Remark 3.8: the formal completion is meromorphic
items.statement: The logarithm of the extension of f̂ to all roots of unity (Corollary 3.7), under mild assumptions, is a meromorphic function log f̂(q) with simple poles at the roots of unity, with residues m^{−2}D_p(ξ) and their images under powers of p^{−2}φ_p.
items.note: Stated without proof and without its assumptions; no layer plans the meromorphic picture of the local sections.

items.name: Local classes and their root-of-unity presentations
items.statement: Locally the modules are indexed by ξ̂ ∈ Im(K_3(K) → K_3(K_p; Z_p) ⊗ Z_p), presented by Theorem 9 as ξ̂ = Σ_ζ a_ζ[ζ] ∈ K_3(K_p) ⊗ Z_p with a_ζ ∈ Z_p, ζ running over the ζ ∈ μ(K_p) with every component ≠ 1 (finding E38).

items.name: The Pochhammer sections Ψ_{[ζ],p} and Ψ_{ξ̂,p} (Definition 3.9)
items.statement: For a prime p and ζ ∈ μ(K_p) with every component ≠ 1 (finding E38): Ψ_{[ζ],p,m}(x) = exp(−Li_2(ζ)/(m² log q)) ε_m([ζ])^{1/m}(q^{m/2}ζ; q^m)_∞^{1/m} ∈ ε_m([ζ])^{1/m}(1 + xK_p[ζ_m][[x]]), q = ζ_m + x, (m, p) = 1; and Ψ_{ξ̂,p} = ∏_ζ Ψ_{[ζ],p}^{a_ζ} for ξ̂ as in (206).

items.name: Theorem 10: the Pochhammer sections are local sections
items.statement: For all ξ̂ as in (205) and p > 3 unramified, Ψ_{ξ̂,p} is an invertible L_p(ξ̂)-section.
items.note: Proved by a pointer to Proposition 2.2 with the factor q^{1/2}; the linear coefficient of Ψ is integral, so the corrected Definition 1.3 is met.

items.name: Local sections by telescoping sums
items.statement: For h ∈ ∏_{(m,p)=1}(1/x)R^∧_p[ζ_m][[x]] with h(ζ_m + x) = (φ_pD_p(ξ) − p²D_p(ξ))/(m²p² log q) + (1/(mp))log((σ_pε(ξ))^p/ε(ξ)) + O(x²) (209), the series log f(q) = (1/m)log ε(ξ) + Σ_{k≥0} (φ_p^k/p^k)[(φ_pD_p(ξ) − p²D_p(ξ))/(m²p^{2+k}log q) + (1/(mp))log(φ_pε(ξ)/ε(ξ)) − h(q^{p^k})] (210) converges and defines an L_p(ξ)-section.
items.note: Review: As printed, (209) has log((σ_pε(ξ))^p/ε(ξ)) and (210) has log(φ_pε(ξ)/ε(ξ)); this alternative proof of Theorem 1 is only sketched ('which is a convergent sum').

items.name: Corollary 3.10: the Pochhammer section is independent of the presentation
items.statement: For p > 3 with p ∤ Δ, the class of Ψ_{ξ̂,p} in H^×_{R^∧_p,ξ̂}/H^×_{R^∧_p} depends only on ξ̂, not on the presentation (206).

items.name: Remark 3.11: specialisations t = q^ν
items.statement: For ν ∈ Z^N the specialisation t_j = q^{mν_j} (at level m) defines f_{A,z,ν}(q) ∈ H_{R[1/√δ],ξ}|_Δ.
items.note: Proof omitted in the paper (finding E46).

items.name: Corollary 3.12: integrality of the constants U^{FGI}_m(1)
items.statement: For m prime to Δ, U^{FGI}_m(1) ∈ R[δ^{−1/2}][ζ_m, ε_m(ξ)^{1/m}]; it is Δ-integral when δ is a unit away from Δ.
items.note: Corrected hypothesis (finding E47).

items.name: The residue formula for the symmetrisation
items.statement: J_A(t,w,q) = Σ_{n∈Z_{≥0}^N} (−q^{1/2})^{nᵀAn}q^{½diag(A)·n}w^{An}t^n/(qw;q)_n expands at q = ζ_m + x into Z[ζ_m][t, w_i^{±1}, (1 − t_i^mP_i(w^m))^{−1}][[x]] with P_i(z) = (−1)^{A_{ii}}(1 − z_i)^{−1}∏_j z_j^{A_{ij}}; Ψ_{A,m}(t,x) = Res_{w^m=z} t^{−1/m}J_A(t^{1/m}, w, ζ_m + x) dw/w, where t_iP_i(z) = 1, and Ψ_{A,m}(t,0) = (1/(δ_A(t)m^N))Σ_{w^m=z}Σ_{n∈(Z/mZ)^N}(−ζ_m^{1/2})^{nᵀAn}ζ_m^{½diag(A)·n}w^{An}t^n/(qw;q)_n, δ_A as in (120).

items.name: Theorem 11: the residue formula computes f_A(t,q)f_A(t,q^{−1})
items.statement: For every m and f_A as in Theorem 3, Ψ_A(t,q) = f_A(t,q)f_A(t,q^{−1}) ∈ Z[ζ_m][[x]][[t^{1/m}]], q = ζ_m + x.
items.note: Coefficients in (223) and (226) (finding E48).

items.name: Theorem 12: descendants of the symmetrisation lie in a Habiro ring
items.statement: Let A be a symmetric integral N×N matrix such that the equations P_i(z) = 1 (i.e. (219) at t = 1) define a reduced zero-dimensional scheme over Q, let z be a solution, K = Q(z), and R = O_K[1/Δ] with Δ as in Theorem 5 (divisible by 6 and disc(K), by the primes of the exceptional integer of Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier Theorem 1.6, and such that every z_j is a unit of R). Then Ψ_{A,μ,ν,z}(q) ∈ H_{R[δ^{−1}]} for all μ, ν ∈ Z^N; this is H_R when δ ∈ R^×.
items.note: Corrected as for Corollary 1.11(a) (findings E18 and E50); some cases are due to F. Wagner.

items.name: Example 4.1: the symmetrised series for A = (3)
items.note: Corrected by the factor t (finding E49) and the inverted primes (finding E50).

items.name: Nahm matrices of the three simplest hyperbolic knots
items.statement: A_{4_1} = [[1,1],[1,1]], A_{5_2} = [[2,1,1],[1,1,0],[1,0,1]] and A_{(−2,3,7)} = [[1,0,1],[0,1,2],[1,2,4]] in Theorem 5 give the asymptotic series of these knots; in general one uses SnapPy quads with B^{−1}A integral and A = I − B^{−1}A.
items.note: Not rechecked in this extraction.

items.name: The rank-one example A = (3): Donaldson–Thomas invariants
items.statement: F(t,q) = Σ_k(−1)^k q^{3k(k+1)/2}t^k/(q;q)_k satisfies F(t,q) − F(qt,q) + q³tF(q³t,q) = 0; its DT invariants c_{n,i} are non-negative and non-zero only for 3n + 1 ≤ i ≤ n² + n + 1 (and c_{1,3} = 1), with the values of (236) for n ≤ 6, and c_{20,142} = 44549701024.
items.note: The table (236) was recomputed in PARI/GP; c_{20,142} was not.

items.name: The rank-one example A = (3): z, V, δ and the leading asymptotics
items.statement: With 1 − z = −tz³: z(t) = Σ_k binom(3k,k)t^k/(2k + 1), V(t) = −Li_2(1 − z) − (3/2)(log z)² = t + (5/4)t² + (28/9)t³ + ⋯, δ(t) = −2t − t/(1 − z(t)) = 1 − 5t − 3t² − 10t³ − ⋯ ∈ Z[[t]], and f̂_1(t,x) = e^{V/log(1+x)}δ^{−1/2}(1 + O(x)) with the coefficient of x^k in f_1(t,x)e^{−V/log(1+x)}δ^{1/2+3k} in Q[t,z].
items.note: Corrected exponent e^{V/log(1+x)} (finding E51).

items.name: The rank-one example A = (3): the Riccati equation and the product for z
items.statement: G(t,q) = F(qt,q)/F(t,q) satisfies 1 − G(t,q) + q³tG(t,q)G(qt,q)G(q²t,q) = 0, lim_{q→1}G(t,q) = z(t), and z(t) = ∏_{n≥1}(1 − t^n)^{−nΣ_i c_{n,i}}.

items.name: The rank-one example A = (3): integrality of G and F^{sym} at q = 1
items.statement: G(t,1+x) = Σ_k g_k(t)x^k with g_0 = z and δ^{3k}g_k ∈ Z[t^{±1}, z]; F^{sym}(t,1+x) = Σ_k f^{sym}_k(t)x^k with δ^{3k+1}f^{sym}_k ∈ Z[t^{±1}, z] (first values (246), (248)); at t = 1, F^{sym}(1,1+x) = 1/δ + (−59z² − 51z + 36)x²/δ⁷ + (−1029z² + 166z + 2026)x³/δ^{10} + O(x⁴) with δ = −z² − z − 2 of norm −23, and F^{sym}(1,q), G(1,q) lie in the Habiro ring of Z[z, 1/(6·23)] and its field of fractions.
items.note: The t = 1 values were rechecked from (248); the inverted primes follow finding E50.

items.name: A relative Habiro ring for the rank-one example
items.statement: F^{sym}(t,q) and G(t,q) are elements of the Habiro ring of the étale map Z[t^{±1}, 1/δ] → Z[t^{±1}, 1/δ][z]/(1 − z + tz³).
items.note: Review: Stated without proof. The Habiro ring of the étale map Z[t^{±1}, 1/δ] → Z[t^{±1}, 1/δ][z]/(1 − z + tz³) is not defined in the paper, and as in finding E50 nothing is proved at 2 and 3.

items.name: Rank-one formulas as polynomials in A
items.locator: §4.2, (251)–(254) and the display between them, pp. 50–51
items.note: Corrected signs in (253) and (254) (findings E52 and E53).

items.name: A torsion example: A = [[8,5],[5,4]]
items.statement: The Nahm equations 1 − z_1 = z_1^8z_2^5, 1 − z_2 = z_1^5z_2^4 have eight solutions in two Galois orbits over the quartic fields defined by z_1^4 + z_1^3 + 3z_1^2 − 3z_1 − 1 = 0, z_2 = (−9z_1^3 − 6z_1^2 − 25z_1 + 37)/5 (discriminant −5²·19, signature (2,1)) and z_1^4 − z_1^3 + 3z_1^2 − 3z_1 + 1 = 0, z_2 = z_1^3 + 3z_1; the real solution in (0,1)² gives a 60-torsion ξ, the series f_{A,z,ν} are Δ-integral, and (f_{A,z,ν})^{60} is observed to lie in H_{O_F[1/(5·19)]} (provably after inverting 6); the element of the second field is not torsion.
items.note: Both solution formulas and the discriminants were rechecked in PARI/GP; see findings E54 ((260)) and E55 (the discriminant).

items.name: Computing the Frobenius of R^∧_p by Hensel lifting
items.statement: Let p ∤ Δ and let ξ ∈ R be a generator of K whose minimal polynomial P satisfies p ∤ disc(P) (equivalently P′(ξ) ∈ (R/pR)^×). Then φ_p(ξ) ∈ R^∧_p is the unique root of P congruent to ξ^p modulo p, computed by Newton iteration: if P(ξ^p + αp) ≡ 0 (mod p^d), then β = −P(ξ^p + αp)/(p^d P′(ξ^p)) ∈ R/pR gives P(ξ^p + αp + βp^d) ≡ 0 (mod p^{d+1}).
items.note: Hensel's lemma itself is mathlib:hensels_lemma; the Frobenius of R^∧_p as a ring automorphism (which exists for every unramified p) is planned in HB.6. Review: the paper derives P′(ξ^p) ∈ (R/pR)^× from 'p unramified' (p. 53), which also needs p ∤ [O_K : Z[ξ]]; counterexample ξ = 5√2 in Q(√2) at p = 5 (finding E78).

items.name: The Besser–de Jeu algorithm for p-adic polylogarithms
items.statement: Li_n(t) is computed from the power series for |t| < 1; at roots of unity ζ ≠ 1 of order prime to p from Li^{(p)}_n(ζ) and Li_n(ζ) = (p^{ns} − 1)^{−1}Σ_{r=0}^{s−1}p^{n(s−r)}Li^{(p)}_n(ζ^{p^r}) (ζ ∈ μ_{p^s−1}); near ζ by Taylor expansion with (t∂_t)^sLi_n = Li_{n−s}; for |t| > 1 by Li_n(z) + (−1)^nLi_n(1/z) = −log(z)^n/n!; near 1 through Li_n(t) − log(t)Li_{n−1}(t)/(n − 1).
items.note: The identity (268) was rechecked by telescoping.

items.name: Example 4.3: Theorem 9 for the cubic field of discriminant −23 at p = 5
items.statement: For K = Q(α), α³ − α² + 1 = 0, z_1 = z_3 = 1 − α², z_2 = z_1² − z_1 + 2 and ξ = [z_1] + [z_2] + [z_3] (the class of 5_2): K_5 ≅ Q_{25} × Q_5, μ(K_5) ≅ μ_{24} × μ_4, and ζ_{24} = lim_s α^{5^{2s}} generates a subgroup of order 24. D_5(ξ) = c_1D_5(ζ_{24}) + c_2D_5(ζ_{24}²) + c_3D_5(ζ_{24}⁶) with c_1 = 1 + 4·5 + 3·5² + ⋯, c_2 = 3 + 5 + ⋯, c_3 = 1 + 5 + 4·5² + ⋯, so ξ = c_1[ζ_{24}] + c_2[ζ_{24}²] + c_3[ζ_{24}⁶] in B(K_5) ⊗ Q_5 (as printed in (275); by the injectivity of D_5 in Theorem 9, an identity in K_3(K_5; Z_5)).
items.note: Recomputed 5-adically in PARI/GP (to 5^12): (271), (274) and the values in (273) are right; the label of the second line of (273) is not (finding E56). The powers ζ_24, ζ_24², ζ_24⁶ have both components ≠ 1 (finding E38).

items.name: The figure-eight knot: series, symmetrisation and a global generator
items.statement: For 4_1 the series Φ(h) = (−3)^{−1/4}(1 + 11h/(24·3√−3) + 697h²/(1152(3√−3)²) + ⋯) (q = e^h) has factorially growing denominators, while Φ(h)Φ(−h) = (−3)^{−1/2}(1 − (q − 1)²/3³ + (q − 1)³/3³ − ⋯) is integral away from 3; the constant terms of the series at ζ_p match the 3-integral value of the symmetrised series up to the Legendre symbol (p/3); f^{4_1}_1(x) = (1 + x)^{1/8}⟨ψ_{0,ζ_6,1}(w_1,x)ψ_{0,ζ_6,1}(w_2,x)⟩_{Λ_{4_1}}; and ⁴√−3 f̂^{4_1}_1(x)(1 + x)^{−1/24}(ζ_6²; 1 + x)_∞^3(1 − ζ_6)^{−3/2} = 1 + (5ζ_6 − 7)x/3³ + (31 − 30ζ_6)x²/3⁵ + (1565ζ_6 − 1444)x³/3⁹ + ⋯ is integral away from 3.
items.note: The coefficient −1/3³ of (q − 1)² was rechecked from (1).

items.name: The 5_2 and (−2,3,7)-pretzel knots: products and symmetrisations
items.statement: The series of 5_2 and of the (−2,3,7)-pretzel knot (common trace field of discriminant −23, scissors congruent) satisfy f^{(5_2)}_1(x)f^{(−2,3,7)}_1(−x/(1 + x)) = c(1 + (−7α² + 20α + 33)x/(2⁴·23) + ⋯) with denominators powers of 2 and 23, where c = 1/√(−6α² + 10α − 4) · 1/√(−24α² + 32α − 26), so c² = 1/((−6α² + 10α − 4)(−24α² + 32α − 26)); f^{5_2}_1(x) = δ^{−1/2}⟨e^wψ_{0,z,1}(w,x)³⟩_{3α−2}, δ = 3α − 2; δ f^{5_2}_1(x)f^{5_2}_1(−x/(1 + x)) = 1 + (465α² − 465α + 54)(x² − x³)/23³ + ⋯; and the 5-adic gluing check (α² + 4α)^5 ≡ α² + 3α + 2 (mod 5) between the constant terms at ζ_5.
items.note: Corrected c (finding E57) and (285) (finding E58); the x² coefficient of (283) was rechecked against (344), and (286) in PARI/GP.

items.name: The 5_2 series divided by the Pochhammer generator is 5-integral
items.statement: For a constant C, C f^{5_2}_1(x)Ψ_{[ζ_{24}],5}(x)^{−c_1}Ψ_{[ζ_{24}²],5}(x)^{−c_2}Ψ_{[ζ_{24}⁶],5}(x)^{−c_3} (c_i as in Example 4.3) has 5-integral coefficients, computed to x^{200}.
items.note: Corrected index f_1 (finding E59).

items.name: The (−2,3,7)-pretzel knot over Q(2cos(2π/7))
items.statement: The perturbative series of the three boundary-parabolic representations of the (−2,3,7)-pretzel knot, with values in K = Q(2cos(2π/7)), give an element of H_{O_K[1/7]}; the Bloch class is 3-torsion, and the denominator of the coefficient of x^{400} is 2^{1997}·3^{596}·7^{466}, improving to 2^{1997}·7^{466} for the cube.
items.note: A numerical observation; the word “denominator” is missing (finding E60). Review: 'H_{O_K[1/7]}' does not fit the paper's own figures: the x^400 coefficient has 3^596 in its denominator before cubing and the cube keeps 2^1997, so the series is a section of the module twisted by the 3-torsion class and only its cube lies in a Habiro ring, with 2 and 3 inverted (finding E73; compare E50).

items.name: Example 4.4: quadratic Gauss sums at roots of unity
items.statement: F_m = (1/m)(Σ_{k∈Z/mZ}ζ_m^{k²})(Σ_kζ_m^{−k²}) = ½(1 + ζ_4^m)(1 + ζ_4^{−m}) equals 1, 0, 1, 2 for m ≡ 1, 2, 3, 0 (mod 4), an element of H_{Z[1/2]}; G_m = (ζ_4/m)(Σ_kζ_m^{k²})² = −½(1 + ζ_4^{−m})² equals i, 0, −i, −2 for m ≡ 1, 2, 3, 0 (mod 4), an element of H_{Z[i,1/2]}.
items.note: Corrected (finding E61). Mathlib has Gauss sums and g² = χ(−1)#R (mathlib:gaussSum, mathlib:gaussSum_sq) but not the sign of the quadratic Gauss sum.

items.name: Example 4.5: the symmetrised Rogers–Ramanujan function
items.statement: J(z,q) = Σ_k q^{k(k+1)}z^{2k}/(qz;q)_k satisfies J(z, ζ_m(1 − u)) ∈ Z[z, (1 − z^m − z^{2m})^{−1}][ζ_m][[u]]; F_m(u) = Σ_{θ^m=ξ}Res_{z=θ}J(z, ζ_m(1 − u))dz/z, ξ² + ξ − 1 = 0, is constant in Q(√5, ζ_m), with −5F_m² − 5F_m = 1 if (m, 5) = 1 and 0 otherwise, the value at ζ_m(1 − u) of an element of H_{Z[1/5]}; H_{Z[1/5]} contains the idempotents χ_N, χ_N(ζ_m) = δ_{v_5(m),N}.
items.note: The relation −5F_1² − 5F_1 = 1 was rechecked by hand.

items.name: Coordinates on the naive Habiro ring and on P_R
items.statement: For a torsion-free ring R, 𝓗_R = lim_n R[q]/(q;q)_n; writing elements as Σ_{n≥1}Σ_{k<n}a_{n,k}q^k(q;q)_{n−1} gives 𝓗_R ≅ ∏_{n>k≥0}R, and writing f_m(u) = Σ_{ℓ≥1}C_ℓ(ζ_m)u^{ℓ−1}, C_ℓ(ζ_m) = Σ_{j<ϕ(m)}γ_{m,ℓ,j}ζ_m^j (q = ζ_m(1 − u)) gives P_R ≅ ∏_{n>0}∏_{mℓ=n, ϕ(m)>j≥0}R. 𝓗_Z = H, but 𝓗_R and H_R differ in general, and 𝓗_Q ≠ 𝓗_Z ⊗ Q.

items.name: The filtrations of 𝓗_R and P_R and their graded pieces
items.statement: 𝓗_{R,N} = (q;q)_{N−1}𝓗_R and P_{R,N} = {f : f_m(u) = O(u^{⌈N/m⌉−1})} are compatible filtrations with split quotients 𝓗^N_R ≅ R[q]/(q;q)_{N−1} (rank N(N − 1)/2) and P^N_R ≅ ⊕_{m≤N}R[ζ_m][u]/(u^{⌈N/m⌉−1}); 𝓗_R = lim 𝓗^N_R, P_R = lim P^N_R, ι(𝓗_{R,N}) ⊆ P_{R,N}, and the graded pieces are 𝓗_{R,N}/𝓗_{R,N+1} ≅ R[q]/(1 − q^N) and P_{R,N}/P_{R,N+1} ≅ ⊕_{mℓ=N}R[ζ_m], both of rank N.
items.note: HC.1–HC.2 plan the completion and its expansions but not these filtrations or their ranks.

items.name: The leading coefficient of (q;q)_{mℓ−1} at ζ_m
items.statement: At q = ζ_m(1 − u), (q;q)_{mℓ−1} = D_{m,ℓ}u^{ℓ−1} + O(u^ℓ) with D_{m,ℓ} = m^{2ℓ−1}(ℓ − 1)!; hence on the graded pieces ι is P(q) ↦ ⊕_{mℓ=N}(D_{m,ℓ}u^{ℓ−1}P(ζ_m) + O(u^ℓ)).
items.note: The paper leaves the calculation to the reader; checked here for (m,ℓ) = (1,2), (2,1), (2,2), (1,3), (3,1).

items.name: Injectivity of ι for torsion-free coefficients
items.statement: For a torsion-free ring R, ι : 𝓗_R → P_R is injective, and it is an isomorphism over Q: H_Z ↪ P_Z and 𝓗_Q ≅ P_Q. The proof: ι respects the filtrations and is injective on the graded pieces, since P(q) ∈ (1 − q^N)R[q] iff P(ζ_m) = 0 for all m | N.
items.note: A proof different from Habiro's, planned in HC.4 through Habiro 2004.

items.name: Proposition 5.1: the index of the naive Habiro ring
items.statement: Let M_N be the integral matrix of ι^N : 𝓗^N_Z → P^N_Z in the bases {q^k(q;q)_{n−1}} and {ζ_m^ju^{ℓ−1}} (block lower triangular, independent of R; (312) shows M_5). Then |det M_N| = D(N − 1), where D(N) := ∏_{n=1}^N D_1(n)D_2(n), D_1(n) = ∏_{mℓ=n}D_{m,ℓ}^{ϕ(m)} = ∏_{mℓ=n}m^{(2ℓ−1)ϕ(m)}(ℓ − 1)!^{ϕ(m)} and D_2(n) = n^{n/2}∏_{m|n}|disc Φ_m|^{−1/2} = ∏_{m|n}((n/m)∏_{p|m}p^{1/(p−1)})^{ϕ(m)/2} ∈ Z. The values D(N) for N ≤ 9 and the factorisations of D(25) and D(100) are as tabulated.
items.note: Corrected index (finding E62); the table and (316) were recomputed in PARI/GP. See finding E83.

items.name: Discriminants of cyclotomic fields
items.statement: |disc Φ_m| = |disc Q(ζ_m)| = m^{ϕ(m)}/∏_{p|m}p^{ϕ(m)/(p−1)}, since Z[ζ_m] is the ring of integers of Q(ζ_m).

items.name: Proposition 5.2: membership in the naive Habiro ring by congruences
items.statement: H ∈ P_R with coordinates γ_{m,ℓ,j} lies in ι(𝓗_R) iff for every N, M*_N(γ_{m,ℓ,j})_{mℓ<N, 0≤j<ϕ(m)} ≡ 0 (mod D(N)), where M*_N := D(N)M_N^{−1} is an integral matrix; equivalently (ι^N)^{−1}(H) ∈ R[q]/(q;q)_{N−1}R[q] for all N.
items.note: No layer plans the congruence (lattice) description of the Habiro ring.

items.name: The first congruences and their identification with Ohtsuki's
items.statement: For N = 5 the conditions are the ten congruences (320); those for N = 4 (321) reduce to γ_{1,1,0} − γ_{2,1,0} + 2γ_{1,2,0} + 4γ_{1,3,0} ≡ 0 (mod 8), γ_{1,1,0} − γ_{3,1,0} − γ_{3,1,1} − 3γ_{1,3,0} ≡ 0 (mod 9) and γ_{1,2,0} + γ_{3,1,1} ≡ 0 (mod 3), and they are the beginnings of Ohtsuki's expansions γ_{2,1,0} = Σ_{k≥0}γ_{1,k+1,0}2^k in R^∧_2 and γ_{3,1,0} + ζ_3γ_{3,1,1} = Σ_{k≥0}γ_{1,k+1,0}(1 − ζ_3)^k in R^∧_3[ζ_3].
items.note: Corrected indices in (323) (finding E63); (321) and (322) were checked in PARI/GP to define the same lattice, of index 216.

items.name: Frobenius automorphisms φ_m of R̂
items.statement: For p ∤ Δ the Frobenius x ↦ x^p of R/pR ≅ ∏_i R/p_iR lifts by Hensel's lemma to automorphisms of R/p^nR; through R/MR ≅ ∏_p R/p^{d_p}R these give φ_p and φ_m = ∏_pφ_p^{v_p(m)} (m ∈ Q^×) on R/MR and on R̂ = lim_M R/MR ≅ ∏_p R_p, lifted to R̂[ζ_n][[x]] fixing ζ_n and x, and φ : P_{R̂} → P_{R̂}, (φf)_m = φ_m(f_m).

items.name: Chinese remainder decomposition of R/MR
items.statement: For M = ∏_p p^{d_p}, R/MR ≅ ∏_p R/p^{d_p}R.

items.name: p-adic completion of a finite Z-algebra
items.statement: R^∧_p := lim_n R/p^nR. If R is a finitely generated Z-module (e.g. Z[ζ_m] or O_K), then R^∧_p ≅ R ⊗_Z Z_p. For R = O_K[1/Δ], R^∧_p ≅ O_K ⊗_Z Z_p when p ∤ Δ, and R^∧_p = 0 when p | Δ (whereas R ⊗_Z Z_p = K ⊗_Q Q_p ≠ 0 then).
items.note: Review: the Mathlib declaration covers finite modules over a Noetherian ring (O_K); the localisation R = O_K[1/Δ] needs the one-line argument R/p^nR = O_K/p^n (p ∤ Δ) or 0 (p | Δ). Finding E77 records the paper's slip.

items.name: Proposition 5.3: the Habiro ring of R through the naive ring of R̂
items.statement: Let R = O_K[1/Δ] with disc(K) | Δ. Then H_R = {H ∈ P_R | φ(H) ∈ ι(𝓗_{R̂})}, where 𝓗_{R̂} is the naive Habiro ring (296) of R̂ = lim_M R/MR and φ is the composite P_R ↪ P_{R̂} → P_{R̂}, (φf)_m = φ_m(f_m); equivalently H_R = P_R ∩ φ^{−1}(ι(𝓗_{R̂})).
items.note: Rests on the last isomorphism of (14) (finding E6).

items.name: Proposition 5.4: membership in H_R by twisted congruences
items.statement: Let R = O_K[1/Δ] with disc(K) | Δ, and let H ∈ P_R have coordinates γ_{m,ℓ,j} ∈ R (m, ℓ ≥ 1, 0 ≤ j < ϕ(m)). Then H ∈ H_R if and only if M*_N(φ_mγ_{m,ℓ,j})_{mℓ<N, 0≤j<ϕ(m)} ≡ 0 (mod D(N)) in R̂ for all N ∈ Z_{>0}, with M*_N as in Proposition 5.2.
items.note: An explicit test for the number-field Habiro ring; no layer plans it.

items.name: Remark 5.5: congruence descriptions of the modules
items.statement: Since Theorem 1 makes the completion Ĥ_{R,ξ} free over H_{R̂}, the modules H_{R,ξ} have descriptions like Proposition 5.4 after dividing by a chosen generator of Ĥ_{R,ξ}.
items.note: No proof is given; no layer plans it.

items.name: Example 5.7: an element of H_{Z[1/2]} not in H_Z
items.statement: The element F ∈ H_Q with F(ζ_m(1 − u)) = 1 for m odd and 0 for m even lies in H_{Z[1/2]} but not H_Z: F(q) = 1 + ¼(−1 + q)(q;q)_1 + ⅛(1 − q + q²)(q;q)_2 + (1/32)(−5 + 2q + q² + 4q³)(q;q)_3 + ⋯; likewise G(q) = F(q²) − F(q), equal to 1 at orders ≡ 2 (mod 4) and 0 otherwise, is ¼(1 − q)(q;q)_1 + ⅛(−1 + q − q²)(q;q)_2 + (1/32)(1 − 2q + 3q² − 4q³)(q;q)_3 + ⋯.
items.note: The printed terms were checked at q = 1, −1, ζ_3 and i.

items.name: Example 5.8: the 5_2 element of the Habiro ring of the cubic field of discriminant −23
items.statement: With J_{5_2}(t,w,q) = Σ_k q^{k(k+1)}w^{2k}t^k/(qw;q)_k³, z = 1 − α² (so z²(1 − z)^{−3} = 1) and Ψ_{5_2,m}(u) = Res_{w^m=z}J_{5_2}(1,w,ζ_m(1 − u))dw/w, one has (3α − 2)Ψ_{5_2,1}(−x) = δf^{5_2}_1(x)f^{5_2}_1(−x/(1 + x)) of (283). The coordinates (345) are not in the image of the naive ring (M_5^{−1} gives denominators 2⁵·3·23⁴), but after the Frobenius twists φ_m they satisfy the congruences of Proposition 5.4 for N = 5, integrally away from 23.
items.note: Uses Proposition 5.4 (missing). The relation with (283) and 1/(3α − 2) = (−9α² + 3α + 2)/23 were rechecked in PARI/GP; (346)–(347) were not.

items.name: Habiro-like series from a polynomial P
items.statement: For P(X) ∈ Z[X], f_P(w,t;q) = Σ_{k≥0}∏_{j=0}^{k−1}P(q^jw)t^k has x-expansions at q = ζ + x whose coefficients are rational functions of t and w, which can be specialised at t = 1: f_P(w,t;1 + x) = 1/(1 − tP(w)) + t²wP(w)P′(w)x/(1 − tP(w))³ + O(x²), so f_P(w,1;1 + x) = 1/(1 − P(w)) + wP(w)P′(w)x/(1 − P(w))³ + O(x²); and f_P(w,1;ζ_m + x) = Σ_k A_{k,m}(w)x^k/(1 − P_m(w^m))^{2k+1} with A_{k,m} ∈ Z[ζ_m, w] and P_m(w) = ∏_{u^m=w}P(u). P_m = P for all m exactly when P(w) = (−w)^a(1 − w)^b, the case of Section 4.1.
items.note: Corrected special form (finding E64). The printed x-coefficients in (349)–(350), tP′(w)/(1 − tP(w))³ and P′(w)/(1 − P(w))³, are wrong: the middle line of (349) drops the factor w, and Σ_k binom(k,2)t^kP^{k−1} = t²P/(1 − tP)³. The correct coefficient is t²wP(w)P′(w)/(1 − tP(w))³, checked for P = w and numerically. See finding E81.

items.name: Residues at the roots of 1 − P_m and the gluing of different fields
items.statement: For α_m with P_m(α_m) = 1, f_{P,m}(x) = Σ_{z^m=α_m}Res_{w=z}f_P(w,1;ζ_m + x)dw/w ∈ O_{P,m}[ζ_m][[x]], O_{P,m} = O_{Q(α_m)}[1/disc(1 − P_m)]; for p ∤ Δ, α_{pm} ↦ α_m gives O_{P,pm}/p ≅ O_{P,m}/p, lifted by Hensel to O_{P,pm}/p^n ≅ O_{P,m}/p^n, which is what the gluing (13) needs.

items.name: Example 5.9: P(X) = −X³ + 8
items.statement: P_m(X) = 8^m − X³ if m ≢ 0 (mod 3) and (2^m − X)³ = −X³ + 3·2^mX² − 3·4^mX + 8^m if 3 | m; O_{P,m} is generated by ξ with ξ³ = 8^m − 1, respectively ξ³ − 3·2^mξ² + 3·4^mξ − (8^m − 1) = (ξ + 1 − 2^m)(ξ² − (2^{m+1} + 1)ξ + 4^m + 2^m + 1) = 0; conjecturally f_{P,m}(x) = 1/21 for m ≢ 0 (mod 3) and 0 otherwise, so that 7f_P would lie in H_{Z[1/3]}.
items.note: Corrected (findings E65 and E66); the value (360) is conjectural in the paper.

items.name: Example 5.10: P(X) = −X³ + 7X² − 14
items.note: Not rechecked in this extraction.

items.name: Theorem 2(ii): the K_3-graded Picard homomorphism
items.statement: Multiplication gives a canonical isomorphism H_{R,ξ} ⊗_{H_R} H_{R,ξ′} ≅ H_{R,ξ+ξ′}; in particular each H_{R,ξ} is an invertible H_R-module, and ξ ↦ H_{R,ξ} is a homomorphism K_3(K) → Pic(H_R), realised at the level of groupoids.
items.note: Split from item 23. The printed proof shows only that products land in H_{R,ξ+ξ′}; the isomorphism, invertibility and the homomorphism to Pic(H_R) are not proved (finding E41).

items.name: Corollary 2.4(b): V, δ and the U_m determine an admissible series
items.statement: For admissible F^{(1)}, F^{(2)} in the same variables t: F^{(1)} = F^{(2)} if and only if V^{(1)} = V^{(2)}, δ^{(1)} = δ^{(2)} and U^{(1)}_m = U^{(2)}_m for all m ≥ 1.
items.note: Split from item 62.

items.name: Corollary 2.4(c): one expansion determines an admissible series
items.statement: For admissible F^{(1)}, F^{(2)} in the same variables t: F^{(1)} = F^{(2)} if and only if f^{(1)}_m = f^{(2)}_m for some (hence every) m ≥ 1.
items.note: Split from item 62.

items.name: Theorem 9(b): K_3(K_p; Z_p) is generated by roots of unity
items.statement: Assume p > 3 and p unramified in K. Then K_3(K_p; Z_p) is generated as a Z_p-module by the classes [ζ], ζ ∈ μ(K_p) with every component ≠ 1.
items.note: Split from item 98 and deduced there from part (a) and Proposition 3.3. In each factor Q_{p^s}, ζ ∧ (1 − ζ) = 0 for ζ ∈ μ ∖ {1}, so [ζ] is a Bloch-group element; ζ = 1 is excluded (finding E38).

items.name: Continuity and the five-term relation of the Bloch–Wigner function
items.statement: D is continuous on C and satisfies D(x) + D(y) = D(xy) + D((1 − y)/(1 − x^{−1})) + D((1 − x)/(1 − y^{−1})) (173); hence D_σ is well defined on B(K).
items.note: Split from item 90. Cited from Bloch and Zagier ([9], [50]).

items.name: Integrality of Li_2 and Li_1 at roots of unity (Besser–de Jeu)
items.statement: For a prime p and a root of unity ζ ≠ 1 of order prime to p: Li_2(ζ) ∈ p²Z_p[ζ] and Li_1(ζ) ∈ pZ_p[ζ].
items.note: Cited from Besser–de Jeu, Math. Comp. 77 (2008), Corollary 4.9. The input of Lemma 3.1 (item 92), and through it of Theorem 9.

items.name: K_3 of an unramified p-adic field (Weibel)
items.statement: For p > 3 unramified in K, K_3(K_p; Z_p) ≅ H¹(K_p, Z_p(2)), a free Z_p-module of rank [K:Q]; it is torsion-free because H⁰(K_p, F_p(2)) = 0 for p > 3.
items.note: Cited from Weibel's K-book [46, Thm. 7.4]. The paper writes 'rank r' without defining r; r = [K:Q] is the local Euler characteristic count.

items.name: Balanced products do not see the polar part of the formal completion
items.statement: Let f = (f_m) satisfy Definition 1.3 locally (formal completion f̂ as in (22)), and let γ_1, …, γ_n, γ′_1, …, γ′_{n′} be positive integers with Σ_k γ_k^{−1} = Σ_k γ′_k^{−1}. At roots of unity of order m prime to ∏_k γ_k ∏_k γ′_k, the product f(q^{γ_1})⋯f(q^{γ_n}) f(q^{−γ′_1})⋯f(q^{−γ′_{n′}}) is unchanged when f is replaced by f̂; in particular f(q^γ)^γ f(q^{−1}) = f̂(q^γ)^γ f̂(q^{−1}) at q = ζ_m + x with (m, γ) = 1. As γ ranges over Z_{>0}, the products f(q^γ)^γ f(q^{−1}) determine f near every root of unity of order prime to 6.
items.note: Used in the proofs of Proposition 1.5(e) and Theorem 2; HB.7 plans multiplication of the modules.

items.name: The level-m q-difference equation of the congruence sums and uniqueness of its solution
items.statement: For A ∈ Z (N = 1; the paper says general N is analogous), m ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ k < m: t^k F_{A,m,k}(t,q), equivalently H_{A,m,k}(t,q) = (−1)^{Ak}q^{Ak(k+1)/2} t^k F_{A,m,k}(t,q)/(q;q)_k, satisfies Σ_{ℓ=0}^m (−1)^ℓ q^{−ℓ(ℓ−1)/2} binom(m,ℓ)_{q^{−1}} σ^ℓ(t^k F) = (−1)^{Am} q^{Am(m+1)/2} t^m σ^{Am}(t^k F), with σt = qt (sign corrected as in finding E30). For q = ζ_{mm′} + x this equation has a unique solution Σ_{j≥0} a_j(x) t^{k+mj} in t^k Q[ζ_{mm′}]((x))[[t^m]] with a_0 = 1: for j ≥ 1, (q^{k+mj+1−m};q)_m a_j = (−1)^{Am} q^{Am(m+1)/2 + Am(k+m(j−1))} a_{j−1}, and (q^{k+mj+1−m};q)_m ≠ 0 (finding E35).
items.locator: §2.4, proof of Theorem 7, (97)–(98), p. 26; §2.7, proof of Theorem 8, (165)–(166), p. 35
items.note: The step behind Theorems 7 and 8 (items 72, 86); signs as corrected by findings E30 and E35.

items.name: Galois shift of the formal Gaussian integrals
items.statement: Let γ_j be the automorphism of Z[ζ_m, t^{±1/m}, z^{±1/m}, 1/δ]/(1 − z − (−1)^A t z^A) sending z_j(t)^{1/m} to ζ_m z_j(t)^{1/m} and fixing S^{(m)}. Then γ_j I_{A,m,k}(t,x) = I_{A,m,k+δ_j}(t,x) (apply γ_j and change variables w ↦ w + h). Hence f^{FGI}_{A,m} = Σ_k I_{A,m,k}(t^{1/m},x) is invariant under every γ_j, and the x-coefficients of its logarithm lie in S^{(m)}_Q.
items.note: Used for Lemma 2.12 (item 78) and in the proof of Theorem 5.

items.name: Integrality of the shift ratios of F_A (proof of Theorem 6)
items.statement: For a symmetric integral N×N matrix A, G_j(t,q) = F_A(σ_j t,q)/F_A(t,q) = ∏_{n≠0}∏_{i∈Z}(q^i t^n;q)_{n_j}^{−c_{n,i}} lies in Z[q^{±1}][[t]] for j = 1, …, N. The G_j satisfy together the system obtained by dividing (33) by F_A (the corrected form of (89), finding E27), which determines them by induction on the t-degree. Consequently log F_A = −Σ_n Σ_ℓ L_n(q^ℓ)t^{ℓn}/(ℓ(1 − q^ℓ)) with L_n(q) ∈ ∩_{i: n_i ≠ 0} ((1 − q)/(1 − q^{n_i}))Z[q^{±1}].
items.note: The integrality input of Theorem 6 (item 67); the system is the corrected (89) of finding E27.

items.name: The intersection identity (57)
items.note: The step from Lemma 2.1 to Proposition 2.2(a) (item 54).

items.name: First-order q-difference equation of the formal Gaussian integrals
items.statement: For ℓ ∈ (Z/mm′Z)^N and j = 1, …, N: I_{A,mm′,ℓ}(t,x) − I_{A,mm′,ℓ}(σ_j t,x) = (−1)^{A_{jj}} t_j q^{A_{jj}} I_{A,mm′,ℓ−δ_j}(∏_i σ_i^{A_{ij}} t, x), where σ_j t = (t_1, …, q t_j, …, t_N), q = ζ_{mm′} + x.
items.note: Lemma 2.15 (item 83), and through it Theorems 8 and 3, rest on it; asserted with references to Bar-Natan–Garoufalidis–Rozansky–Thurston and Garoufalidis–Storzer–Wheeler.

items.name: The products ψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ,ν} and the uniqueness of their q-difference system
items.statement: Let N = 1 (the paper omits N > 1 as analogous), A ∈ Z, and ψ_{A,μ}(t,q) = F_A(q^μt, q) (211). For γ ∈ Z_{>0}, μ = (μ_1,…,μ_γ) ∈ Z^γ and ν ∈ Z put ψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ,ν}(t,q) = ψ_{A,μ_1}(t^γ,q^γ)⋯ψ_{A,μ_γ}(t^γ,q^γ)ψ_{A,ν}(t,q^{−1}) ((212), corrected by finding E43). Then ψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ,ν} − ψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ+δ_i,ν} = (−1)^A q^{γ(A+μ_i)}t^γψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ+Aδ_i,ν} (i = 1,…,γ), ψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ,ν} − ψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ,ν+1} = (−1)^A q^{−(A+ν)}tψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ,ν+A}, and ψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ,ν}(qt,q) = ψ^{(γ)}_{A,μ+(1,…,1),ν−1}(t,q) ((213), corrected by E43). This system has a unique solution among families of power series in t of the form 1 + O(t).
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Theorem 5, (211)–(213) and the paragraph after them, pp. 43–44
items.note: How the proof of Theorem 5 obtains the gluing (24); corrected by finding E43.

items.name: Constant terms of the Nahm-sum series (Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier Theorem 1.6, with Hutchinson)
items.statement: For a non-degenerate solution z of the Nahm equations of A with Bloch element ξ ∈ B(K), and m prime to Δ (Δ containing 2, 3 and the primes of the exceptional integer of CGZ Theorem 1.6 for K), the constant term of f_{A,z,m}(x) is δ^{−1/2}ε_m(ξ)^{1/m} times an element of K[ζ_m]. Cited from Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 56 (2023), Theorem 1.6 with their displays (12)–(13); (13) is proved by Hutchinson, J. Algebra 649 (2024).
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Theorem 5, first paragraph, p. 43
items.note: Cited; HB.2 plans CGZ Theorem 1.6 and Hutchinson's refinement (finding E42 corrects the attribution).

items.name: The Kashaev–Mangazeev–Stroganov identity as used in Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier
items.statement: If rξ = 0 in K_3(K), then (by Suslin's surjection K_3(K) → B(K)) the image of ξ in B(K) is a sum of five-term relations. The five-term identity of Kashaev–Mangazeev–Stroganov (Int. J. Modern Phys. A 8 (1993)) for the cyclic quantum dilogarithm, as used in Calegari–Garoufalidis–Zagier, then shows that the constant term of f_{A,z}(q)^r at ζ_m lies in S^{(m)} for every m, not only for m prime to Δ.
items.locator: §3.3, proof of Corollary 1.11, last paragraph, p. 44
items.note: Cited. HB.2 plans the five-term identity of the cyclic quantum dilogarithm; the accepted HabiroNahmSeries packet already uses the identity for Corollary 1.11(b).

items.name: The families f_{A,μ,ν} and Ψ_{A,μ,ν} and their common q-difference system
items.statement: For μ, ν ∈ Z^N: f_{A,μ,ν}(t,q) = f_A(q^{mμ}t, q)f_A(q^{−mν}t, q^{−1}) and Ψ_{A,μ,ν}(t,q) = Res_{w^m=z} q^ν w^{μ+ν} t_1^{−1/m}⋯t_N^{−1/m} J_A(q^μt^{1/m}, w, ζ_m + x) dw/w (222); Ψ_{A,μ,ν,z}(q) is Ψ_{A,μ,ν} at t = 1 along a solution z of (219). For N = 1 both families satisfy f_{A,μ,ν} − f_{A,μ+1,ν} = (−1)^A q^{A+μ}t^{1/m}f_{A,μ+A,ν}, f_{A,μ,ν} − f_{A,μ,ν+1} = (−1)^A q^{−(A+ν)}t^{1/m}f_{A,μ,ν+A} and f_{A,μ,ν}(q^mt,q) = f_{A,μ+1,ν−1}(t,q) ((223) with the coefficients corrected by finding E48; for Ψ via the J_A-equations (224)). A solution Σ_k a_{μ,ν,k}(q)t^{k/m} ∈ Z[ζ_m][[x]][[t^{1/m}]] (225) is determined by a_{0,0,0} through (226).
items.note: Theorem 12 (item 113) is stated for Ψ_{A,μ,ν,z}, which only (222) defines; coefficients corrected by finding E48.

prerequisites.citation: M. Kontsevich and Y. Soibelman, Cohomological Hall algebra, exponential Hodge structures and motivic Donaldson–Thomas invariants, Commun. Number Theory Phys. 5 (2011)
prerequisites.why: Admissible series (Definition 1.7) and the admissibility of the Nahm sums F_A (their Theorem 9 in §6.1), cited for Theorem 6; the paper reproves it from the q-difference equations, but the Donaldson–Thomas interpretation is theirs.

prerequisites.citation: A. I. Efimov, Cohomological Hall algebra of a symmetric quiver, Compos. Math. 148 (2012)
prerequisites.why: Cited with Kontsevich–Soibelman for Theorem 6, and the source of the positivity of the DT invariants seen in (236).

prerequisites.citation: R. Coleman, Dilogarithms, regulators and p-adic L-functions, Invent. Math. 69 (1982)
prerequisites.why: The p-adic dilogarithm D_p and its analytic continuation along Frobenius, and the integrality of Li^{(p)}_n (Proposition 6.2), used in §§1.5, 2.1 and 3.1.

prerequisites.citation: A. Besser and R. de Jeu, Li^(p)-service? An algorithm for computing p-adic polylogarithms, Math. Comp. 77 (2008)
prerequisites.why: Corollary 4.9 (Li_2(ζ) ∈ p²Z_p[ζ]) is the input of Lemma 3.1 and so of Theorem 9; Proposition 4.2 and the algorithm are used for the computations of §4.4.

prerequisites.citation: T. Dimofte and S. Garoufalidis, The quantum content of the gluing equations, Geom. Topol. 17 (2013)
prerequisites.why: The formal-Gaussian perturbative series at q near 1 from Neumann–Zagier data (§§1.8, 2.5), which Theorem 3 identifies with the admissible series.

prerequisites.citation: T. Dimofte and S. Garoufalidis, Quantum modularity and complex Chern–Simons theory, Commun. Number Theory Phys. 12 (2018)
prerequisites.why: The perturbative series at arbitrary roots of unity (§§1.6, 1.8, 2.5), the level-m version of the formal-Gaussian series.

prerequisites.citation: S. Garoufalidis, M. Storzer and C. Wheeler, Perturbative invariants of cusped hyperbolic 3-manifolds (2023)
prerequisites.why: Cited for the m-periodicity of the Gaussian integrals I_{A,m,k} (needed for Definition 2.11) and for the computation of the 4_1 series (276).

prerequisites.citation: S. Garoufalidis and D. Zagier, Knots and their related q-series, SIGMA 19 (2023) 082
prerequisites.why: The numerical experiments and the matrix of the (−2,3,7)-pretzel knot (Remark 4.2, §4.6) come from it.

prerequisites.citation: S. Garoufalidis and T. T. Q. Lê, From 3-dimensional skein theory to functions near Q (2023)
prerequisites.why: The detailed account of the Habiro ring and of functions near roots of unity that §1.3 refers to.

prerequisites.citation: F. Rodriguez Villegas, A refinement of the A-polynomial of quivers (2011)
prerequisites.why: The hypergeometric solution (76)–(77) of the t-deformed Nahm equations.

routes.reason: Section 5.1 of GSWZ describes the classical Habiro ring inside the functions near roots of unity by explicit congruences: the filtrations by (q;q)_{N−1} and by order of vanishing, the leading coefficients D_{m,ℓ} = m^{2ℓ−1}(ℓ − 1)!, the index formula of Proposition 5.1 (corrected: |det M_N| = D(N − 1)) and the membership test of Proposition 5.2, whose first cases are Ohtsuki’s congruences. HC.2 (expansions and coefficient algorithms) and HC.4 (connectedness and injectivity) are where these belong: they give a finite-precision, lattice-theoretic form of the completion and a second proof of Habiro’s injectivity, and Examples 5.6–5.7 are acceptance tests for HC.6. Nothing here needs a new roadmap.

HB.6 and HB.7 are built on GSWZ Definitions 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4 and Theorems 1–2. Three statements of the paper are not yet in their plans: the twisted-congruence membership test for H_R (Proposition 5.4, which Example 5.8 uses on the cubic field of discriminant −23), its analogue for the modules after dividing by a local generator (Remark 5.5), and the meromorphic picture of the formal completion of a local section (Remark 3.8). They extend the ring and module layers directly and need nothing outside them. The route also carries the corrections to Definition 1.3 (E9), Remark 1.2 (E5), footnote 1 (E2) and the unproved isomorphism of Theorem 2 (E41), which the layers must use.

HabiroNahmSeries formalises GSWZ Theorems 3–8 and 11–12 (HB.8–HB.9) and their examples (HB.10). Section 5.4 of the paper adds Habiro-like elements from q-hypergeometric sums Σ∏P(q^jw)t^k, whose expansions at different roots of unity live over different fields that become isomorphic after p-adic completion; for P = (−w)^a(1 − w)^b they are exactly the residue construction of §4.1 (Theorems 11–12). They are examples of the same q-difference and residue machinery, so HB.10 (explicit examples and boundaries) is their place, with the corrected formulas (E64–E66) and the conjectural status of (360) kept.

D.3 is GSWZ Theorem 9 and follows its four-step proof. The paper is its source, and this route records what the layer has to supply beyond the printed argument: the containment D_p(K_3(K_p; Z_p)) ⊆ p²O and the extension of D_p to the p-completed group are asserted, not proved (E39); the spanning set must exclude ζ = 1 and use ord(ζ)[ζ] (E38); and Example 4.3, recomputed here 5-adically, is a ready acceptance test once the label in (273) is corrected (E56).

sourceIssues.locator: §1.3, p. 5 (arXiv 2412.04241v2; the same text is in v1)
sourceIssues.printed: The source credits Habiro [27] with proving injectivity of (6), including every factor ιm : HZ → Z[ζm][[x]], and characterizing its image as families fm(x) = (ιm f)(x) satisfying arithmetic gluing. It presents this as an extension of Ohtsuki’s earlier work [39].
sourceIssues.correction: Habiro [27] proves the injectivity (Theorems 5.2 and 6.1 there). The description of the image by the gluing (9) is not in [27] and needs a proof. One route is the p-adic splitting ℍ_{Z_p} ≅ ∏_{(m,p)=1} Z_p[ζm][[x]] of the naive Habiro ring, which (14) presupposes but does not prove (finding E6), together with the congruence description of §5.1 (Proposition 5.2).
sourceIssues.reason: [27] is Habiro, Cyclotomic completions of polynomial rings, Publ. RIMS 40 (2004). Its results are the injectivity of restriction, expansion and evaluation maps (Theorems 4.1, 5.2, 6.1–6.3, 7.1), localisation (Propositions 7.2–7.3) and non-surjectivity (§7.4); it says nothing about the image of the Taylor maps or about p-adic re-expansion. The identification of HZ with the families satisfying (9) is used for HZ[1/∆] in §1.4 and in Proposition 5.3.

review.reason: The quoted sentence is on p. 5 of v2 (LaTeX line 595) and is unchanged from v1 (a diff of the v1 and v2 LaTeX changes only the abstract, the prologue, the re-indexing of (4), the new §1.8 and one sentence of §4.2, none of which touches the passages of E1–E22). I read Habiro's arXiv preprint math/0209324 and the published Publ. RIMS 40 (2004) version. Both prove only injectivity and related results: published Theorem 4.1 (ρ), Theorem 5.2 (expansion at ζ), Corollary 5.1 (integral domain), Theorems 6.1–6.3 (values), §7. Neither contains any description of the image or any p-adic re-expansion, and GSWZ never prove it either: §5.1 only proves that ι is injective and gives the congruences of Proposition 5.2, while §5 just asserts that ℍ_Z and 𝓗_Z 'can be identified canonically'. The theorem numbers quoted in the finding match the published version, which numbers theorems, lemmas and corollaries separately.
