review.reason: Footnote 1 on p. 6 reads a ↦ (φm a)m with φm = ∏p φp^{vp(m)}, and v1 has the same text. For a constant family (cm), gluing (13) says cm = φp(cpm). With cm = φm(a) this becomes φm(a) = φp²φm(a). For K = Q(ζ5), a = ζ5 and (p,m) = (2,1) I get c1 = ζ5 but φ2(c2) = φ2(ζ5²) = ζ5^4, so the family does not glue. With cm = φm^{−1}(a) we get φp(φ_{pm}^{−1}a) = φm^{−1}a, so it glues for every p. The corrected family is also the one that (15) and Proposition 5.3 need, since φm(Hm) must be the constant a. The restriction to p ∤ ∆ is harmless, because (13) is empty for p | ∆.

sourceIssues.locator: §1.4, paragraph after Definition 1.1, p. 7 (arXiv 2412.04241v2; the same text is in v1)
sourceIssues.printed: It claims HR has an equivalent construction: glue R[ζm][[q−ζm]] over Z[ζm][[q−ζm]] with Frobenius twists after p-adic completion to obtain a finite étale algebra over HZ[1/∆]. It concludes HR is finitely generated and projective over HZ[1/∆], with rank r = [K : Q]. It justifies this via p-completion and the rank r of Rp[ζm]JxK over Zp[ζm]JxK.
sourceIssues.correction: A claim that needs a proof or a reference: that the gluing construction agrees with Definition 1.1, and that finite projectivity of rank r descends from the p-completions to the non-Noetherian ring HZ[1/∆]. The atlas plans both in HabiroRings HR.4–HR.5 through the relative Habiro ring of an étale map (F. Wagner, arXiv:2510.04782v2, §2, whose Corollary 2.13 the atlas cites for the comparison; not checked here).
sourceIssues.reason: No proof or reference is given. Projectivity cannot be read off from the p-completions alone: one needs that 𝓗_R is recovered from them (the square (15)) and descent of finite projective modules along it. The equivalence of the two definitions also rests on the unproved identification of the p-adically glued families with the naive Habiro ring (finding E6). The rank statement is used in the remark after Corollary 1.11 ('the above constructions presumably give a spanning set for HR').

review.reason: The passage is on p. 7 of v2, and v1 has the same text. review.reason: Remark 1.2 on p. 7 says unconditionally that 𝓗_R is not an integral domain, and v1 has the same text. For K = Q, disc K = 1, so ∆ = 1 is allowed by the definition on p. 6. Then 𝓗_R = 𝓗_Z is Habiro's ring, an integral domain by published Corollary 5.1 of Habiro 2004, which I checked. For ∆ > 1 a prime p | ∆ separates the class of 1 from the class of p, so the ring splits and the remark holds. The introduction to §1.4 states the intended condition 'if ∆ ≠ 1', so misprint is the right kind.

sourceIssues.locator: Remark 1.2, p. 7 (arXiv 2412.04241v2; the same text is in v1)
sourceIssues.printed: It describes HR as a product of integral domains, possibly infinitely many. The factors correspond to classes in N for the relation generated by m ∼∆ pm at primes p that do not divide ∆.
sourceIssues.correction: HR is the product over these classes c of the rings HR|c of families supported on c. The factor of the class of 1, HR|∆, is an integral domain, and so is the factor of the class of d when K ∩ Q(ζd) = Q; a factor can have non-trivial idempotents when K meets Q(ζd).
sourceIssues.reason: R[ζm] means R ⊗Z Z[ζm] (the rank statement on p. 7 needs this). For K = Q(i), ∆ = 12 and R = Z[i, 1/6], the class of 4 is {4m′ : (m′, 6) = 1}, and e4m′ := (1 − i^{m′} ⊗ ζ4)/2 ∈ R ⊗ Z[ζ4m′] is an idempotent other than 0 and 1, since (i^{m′} ⊗ ζ4)² = 1 for odd m′. The constant family (e4m′) satisfies (13) at every p ∤ 12: φp(i) = i^p and p² ≡ 1 (mod 4) give φp(e4pm′) = e4m′, and constants are unchanged by re-expansion. So the factor of this class is not a domain.

review.reason: The sentence is on p. 7, and v1 has the same text. R[ζm] has to mean R ⊗_Z Z[ζm]: the Galois-invariance in (8), the Frobenius in (13) (which must fix ζpm while acting on R) and the rank-r statement on p. 7 all require this. For K = Q(i), ∆ = 12 and R = Z[i,1/6], the class of 4 is {4m′ : (m′,6) = 1}. For odd m′, u = i^{m′}⊗ζ4 satisfies u² = (−1)^{m′+1} = 1, so e = (1−u)/2 is an idempotent other than 0 and 1. Since φp(i) = i^p and p² ≡ 1 (mod 4) for p ≥ 5, φp(e_{4pm′}) = e_{4m′}, so this constant family satisfies (13). The factor on that class is therefore not a domain. I also checked the correction's positive claim: ι1 is injective on the class of 1 by induction along the gluing, and R⊗Z[ζm] is a domain there, so 𝓗_R|∆ is a domain.

sourceIssues.locator: (14), §1.4, p. 7 (arXiv 2412.04241v2; the same text is in v1)
sourceIssues.printed: It asserts (14): (HR)p ≅ {families of R∧p[ζm][[x]]-series, m ≥ 1, glued by re-expansion using x ↦ x + ζmp − ζm} ≅ ∏_{m≥1,(m,p)=1} R∧p[ζm][[x]] ≅ HRp. Its justification is that expansions at distinct roots with orders prime to p have no gluing conditions between them.
sourceIssues.correction: The stated reason proves only the middle isomorphism. The first (the p-adic completion of the non-Noetherian ring 𝓗_R) needs a proof. The last term is the calligraphic 𝓗_{R_p} of Definition 1.1 over R_p, so as printed the last isomorphism restates the middle one. What is used but never proved is that these glued families are exactly ι(ℍ_{R_p}) for the naive Habiro ring ℍ_{R_p} = lim R_p[q]/(q;q)_n of (296), i.e. ℍ_{R_p} ≅ ∏_{(m,p)=1} R∧p[ζm][[x]]. This can be proved from the Chinese remainder splitting of the completion of Z_p[q] over the classes {mp^k} and its identification with Z_p[ζm][[q − ζm]] ((p, Φm)-adic completion and Hensel's lemma).
sourceIssues.reason: Several statements rest on identifying the glued families over R∧p with ι(ℍ_{R∧p}): Proposition 5.3, which restates Definition 1.1 as 𝓗_R = P_R ∩ φ^{−1}(ι(ℍ_R̂)); the claim after (15) that 𝓗_R̂ ≅ 𝓗_{Z[1/∆]} ⊗ R̂; and the identification of 𝓗_Z with Habiro's ring. No proof or reference is given for this identification, and the first isomorphism of (14) is likewise unproved.

review.reason: The display is (14) on p. 7, and v1 has the same text. The stated reason ('no gluing constraints …') justifies only the middle isomorphism. The first isomorphism, the p-adic completion of the non-Noetherian ring 𝓗_R, is not proved anywhere. The finding misreads the last term, however. The rendered PDF and the LaTeX (\calH_{R_p}) show the calligraphic 𝓗_{R_p}, i.e. Definition 1.1 over R_p, where only p glues, not the naive ring ℍ_{R_p} of (296). As printed, the last isomorphism therefore restates the middle one. The genuinely missing step is that the glued families over R_p are exactly ι(ℍ_{R_p}). Proposition 5.3 (𝓗_R̂ = φ^{−1}(ι(ℍ_R̂))), the claim after (15) and the identification 𝓗_Z = Habiro's ring all use this step.

sourceIssues.reason: Take K = Q, ξ = 0 (εm = 1, Dp = 0), p = 5 and fm := (1 + x/ζm)^{1/5} for m prime to 5. The constant term is 1 and (21) holds exactly, because φp f(q^p)/f(q)^p = (1 + x/ζm)^{5/5}/(1 + x/ζm)^{5/5} = 1; but f1 = 1 + x/5 − 2x²/25 + ⋯ ∉ Z5[[x]]. So HZ∧5,0 contains 1 and f; since 1 + x has no 5th root in the normal domain Z5[[x]], f1 is not in its fraction field, 1 and f are independent over HZ∧5, and HZ∧5,0 is not free of rank one. Theorem 1 thus fails for ξ = 0 with (20) as printed; its proof (“Combining Theorem 10 with Corollary 3.5”) uses Corollary 3.5, which needs the linear coefficient integral.

sourceIssues.locator: §1.4, sentence after (15), p. 7 (arXiv 2412.04241v2; the same text is in v1)
sourceIssues.printed: The source asserts 𝓗_R̂ ≅ ∏_p 𝓗_{R∧p}. It describes 𝓗_R as the intersection of P_R with 𝓗_R̂ inside P_R̂ and gives 𝓗_R̂ ≅ 𝓗_{Z[1/∆]} ⊗_Z R̂.
sourceIssues.correction: 𝓗_R̂ ≅ 𝓗_{Z[1/∆]} ⊗̂_Z R̂, a completed tensor product (e.g. ∏_p (𝓗_{Z[1/∆]} ⊗ R)∧_p), not the plain tensor product.
sourceIssues.reason: Take K = Q and ∆ = 1, which the definition on p. 6 allows, so R̂ = Ẑ. The paper identifies 𝓗_Z with ι(ℍ_Z), and (hdecomp) in §5.1 gives ℍ_R ≅ ∏_{n>k≥0} R in coordinates compatible with base change. So the composite 𝓗_Z ⊗_Z Ẑ → 𝓗_Ẑ → 𝓗_{Z_p} has image ι of the image of (∏ Z) ⊗ Z_p → ∏ Z_p = ℍ_{Z_p}. Here ι is injective (§5.1), and ι(ℍ_{Z_p}) ⊂ 𝓗_{Z_p}. That map is not surjective: every element in its image has all coordinates in one finitely generated Z-submodule of Z_p, while Z_p has uncountable Z-rank. So the plain tensor product is not isomorphic to 𝓗_Ẑ via the natural map, and a completed tensor product must be meant. Nothing later uses the plain form.
